content.text:
The preview lifecycle work (S9) is reviewed and committed, with its sign-off queued behind the MCP server change (S5). Neither is merged yet. Both features are now with workers.

**S9 (preview lifecycle):**
- One state machine tracks each preview run: absent, starting, running, stale, stopping, stopped.
- Effect now owns the child processes, port checks, signal handlers and cleanup.
- Readiness and stop waits use Effect's scheduling instead of sleep loops. The preview code now has no raw timers.
- A new start lock means two simultaneous starts end with exactly one owner.
- I removed one wrapper that passed a yes/no straight through the machine without deciding anything.
- I also rebased S9 onto S5, so its sign-off covers the exact tree it will merge as.
- One thing to watch: the launcher now returns an exit code instead of calling `process.exit`. The existing preview test will show whether the process still ends on its own.

**Sign-off queue, one at a time, each waiting for load below 6:** S5 first, then S9.

**Now running in parallel:**
- [S7 source-to-element](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A0c582ed3-41bf-4dea-92b8-d5c7f0730087):
  - Development builds tag each HTML element with the file and line that rendered it.
  - Selecting an element shows its source under Details, and comments and work requests carry it.
  - `civic elements <file>` works the other way, from a file or a diff to the elements it renders.
  - The first test runs on CIVIC's own screens.
- [S8 backend coverage](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3Ab264f09d-7f42-4352-ac78-dc179f103a29):
  - The server routes and functions each journey reaches are worked out from the code and from recorded runs, never typed by hand.
  - There's a server section in the coverage panel and `civic coverage --backend`.
  - A test plants one deliberately unreached server function and checks that the report names it.

I'll add the MCP tools for both features myself once S5 lands.

I'm checking whether the `source` references would need changing too, and I also need to see whether the production flag ever gets set for builds, since the transform as written tags everything regardless of mode. The returned null source map could also cause small column drift in stack traces for tagged UI files, which I think is tolerable for now.

Production builds still get tagged because the transform never passes its production flag, and S7 overloads the existing `source` field with file locations, which is confusing. I'm checking how widely that field is used next.

content.text:
Source-to-element (S7) is reviewed, corrected and committed, but not merged. Its full sign-off, including the browser check on CIVIC's own screens, hasn't run.

**What S7 does:**
- In development, each HTML element in a project's own source gets the file, line and column that drew it. Production builds are never tagged, because the plugin only runs on the dev server.
- Selecting an element in the review overlay or on the canvas shows "Code location" under Details. Comments and work requests keep it, so the agent's work order names the file to open.
- `civic elements <file>[:<from>-<to>]` goes the other way, from a file or line range to the captured elements it renders. A helper turns a diff's changed lines into those ranges.

**What I changed:** S7 had stored the location in the field that already records where a record came from (which tool, which importer, which git line). That made the field's `line` mean two different things. It now has its own `location` field, with its own check that paths stay inside the repo.

**Test status:**
- Type checks and the lint baseline pass.
- The location and diff tests pass.
- The tagging test passes.
- The browser check on CIVIC's own screens, and the full suites, run in the sign-off.

**Load:** it has stayed at 8–9 for over half an hour. The cause is Orca's Playwright test runs in its own worktrees, not CIVIC. I'm keeping to the "below 6" rule, so the S5 sign-off, then S9, then S7, are queued behind it.

content.text:
Backend coverage (S8) came back unfinished. I've handed it to a new worker to complete; nothing new is merged.

**What the first worker built:**
- **Inventory:** CIVIC lists every server function a project defines, read from the code.
- **New hook for projects:** a project whose server has HTTP routes or RPCs can now report them to CIVIC as a generated list. This is a small, documented addition to what a project tells CIVIC.
- **Report:** recorded and replayed runs are turned into "which operations each journey reached". Only passing replays count; a replay that went wrong counts up to the step where it did.
- **Where you see it:** `civic coverage --backend`, and a new server section in the coverage panel.
- **What's missing:** the two examples with HTTP routes (Tasks and Team board) don't produce their route lists yet. Nothing was type-checked, linted or tested.

**What I did:** committed that work as a work-in-progress commit on its own branch. The new worker, [S8 finish backend coverage](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3Ac02542bd-5e08-4552-b856-a191a28e7516), starts from it. It is to:
- read those route lists from the examples' own server code, never from a list typed into CIVIC;
- make the code pass type checks and the shrink-only lint baseline;
- run the browser test that plants one unreached operation and checks the report names exactly that one.

My checkout is back on the controller branch.

**Waiting to sign off, one at a time:**
1. The MCP server on Effect (S5)
2. The preview lifecycle (S9)
3. Source-to-element (S7)

The machine has stayed at about load 8 for over half an hour. Orca's test runs are the cause.

import path from 'node:path'
import { parseSync } from 'vite'

export const tagSources = (input, id, project, production = false) => {
  let code = input
  const file = id.split('?')[0]
  if (production || !/\.[jt]sx$/u.test(file) || !project.sources.some(root => file === root || file.startsWith(root + '/'))) return code
  const relative = path.relative(project.root, file)
  if (relative.startsWith('../')) return code

content.text:
Source-to-element (S7) failed its sign-off a second time and isn't merged yet. The fix for that failure is now in, and the browser check that failed passes.

**What went wrong:** the browser check found no tagged elements on CIVIC's own screens; the tags never reached the page. React's Vite plugin compiles JSX in an early step that runs before CIVIC's tagging step, and changing plugin order can't fix that because both run in the same early group. So the tagger never saw any JSX to tag. The worker hadn't been able to run this check, so this is the first time anything tested it.

**The fix:** tagging now happens when the file is read in, before any plugin compiles it, and only for files in the project's own source folders. I also removed the leftover "production" option, since the plugin only ever runs on the dev server.

**Verified:**
- The connector checks pass (66 of 66).
- The browser check on CIVIC's own screens passes: picking an element gives back the right file and line.
- The lint baseline is clean.

The full sign-off is running again. If it passes, I'll merge the feature together with the `elements` MCP tool. The worker finishing backend coverage (S8) is still running.

content.text:
Backend coverage (S8) works and its focused tests pass, but it's held back by 23 new lint findings, so it isn't merged.

**What S8 now does:**
- **Tasks and Team board:** both examples now handle their requests from route tables they define themselves (3 and 5 routes). CIVIC reads its list of routes from those same tables, so nobody keeps a second list by hand.
- **Reading list:** its server functions are found automatically from its code.
- **What counts as reached:** a route call only counts as reached by a journey if it succeeded; a response of 400 or above doesn't count. Routes with parameters, such as `/tasks/:id`, are matched properly.
- **For agents:** a `backend_coverage` MCP tool gives the same answer as `civic coverage --backend`, and a test checks the two match.

**Tests that passed:**
- Type checks
- The backend coverage and route tests (5)
- The runtime bridge tests (8)
- The browser record-and-replay flows for Tasks, Team board and Reading list

**What's holding it back:** 23 lint findings grew past the shrink-only baseline. They're mechanical: unchecked `!`, a missing regex flag, a shadowed name, `await` inside a loop. A new worker, [S8 lint cleanup](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A16209525-2cb7-42a2-8644-ba7b626bdb62), is fixing them in the code. It may not raise the baseline or switch rules off.

**Something the worker found, not yet checked by me:** replaying a recorded run that ticks a checkbox may compare against the wrong state. This was there before S8, and I'll look into it after these merges.

Source-to-element (S7) is still in its sign-off.

content.content:
## Implementation Units

### U1. Characterize journal and closure boundaries

**Goal:** Bind the existing recovery guarantees before changing resource ownership.
**Requirements:** R8–R10; AE4–AE7. **Dependencies:** None.
**Files:** `packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.check.mjs`, new `packages/canvas/server/runtime-lifecycle.check.mjs`, and small deterministic test fixtures under `packages/canvas/server/check-fixtures/`.
**Approach:** Extend the current backend fixtures with controlled worker and persistence barriers. Keep tests at actual journal and worker boundaries rather than duplicating internal state-machine logic.
**Execution note:** Add characterization coverage before modifying `runtime-service.mjs`.
**Test scenarios:**

1. Covers AE5. Drop a completed write response, close and restore, then resend the same intent and obtain the same receipt with one reconstructed write.
2. Covers AE6. Reopen a live run, send its previous owner's close lease and keep the replacement owner usable.
3. Covers AE7. Change source, seed or a replayed result and refuse restore while retaining the original journal.
4. Kill a fixture worker after intent persistence but before completion persistence; restore only completed entries and require explicit resend for the unfinished step.
5. Exercise existing account, reset, timezone and credential-redaction behavior across closure and restore.

**Verification:** Existing and new journal checks establish the R8–R10 baseline; no production behavior changes in this unit.

### U2. Add lifecycle decisions and scoped execution

**Goal:** Introduce one owner for host and run transitions without another durable store.
**Requirements:** R4, R5, R8–R10, R12. **Dependencies:** U1.
**Files:** New `packages/canvas/server/server-lifecycle.ts`, `packages/canvas/server/run-lifecycle.ts`, `packages/canvas/server/lifecycle.test.ts`, `packages/canvas/server/lifecycle-scope.test.ts`, `packages/canvas/tsconfig.server.json`; `packages/canvas/package.json`, `packages/canvas/vitest.config.ts` and `packages/pnpm-lock.yaml`.
**Approach:** Implement KTD2 and KTD5 with pure XState transitions and Effect-owned schedules. Serialize state changes with attach, expiry and stop events in the same owner queue. Keep host time independent of a run's synthetic clock.
**Test scenarios:**

1. Attach two clients, release either and remain serving; expire the final client and enter waiting.
2. Covers AE3. Reattach before the grace boundary and cancel that shutdown generation; an old timer or release cannot affect the replacement.
3. Run all deadlines under an injected clock, including startup with no client and no new work after stopping begins.
4. Interrupt a scoped task and verify finalizers settle once; a second stop request returns the same cleanup outcome.
5. Advance synthetic run time without changing real client expiry.

**Verification:** State and scope tests enforce KTD2, KTD5 and KTD7 deterministically without worker processes.

### U3. Supervise the existing run service

**Goal:** Give runs bounded, awaitable closure while preserving their public contract.
**Requirements:** R5, R8–R10, R13. **Dependencies:** U1, U2.
**Files:** `packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.mjs`, `packages/canvas/server/runtime-worker.mjs`, `packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.check.mjs`, `packages/canvas/server/runtime-lifecycle.check.mjs`; a scoped execution module if needed under `packages/canvas/server/`.
**Approach:** Keep validation and journal decisions in their existing owner. Place worker acquisition, listeners, expiry and per-run queues under scoped ownership. Add the stop fence before draining and cover pending spawn/restore paths. Retain the exported handle/close facade and existing limit values.
**Test scenarios:**

1. Covers AE4. Stop during a changing operation that finishes before the deadline and save its complete receipt before worker exit.
2. Stop during a hung operation, terminate within KTD5 and retain no false completion.
3. Race stop with worker creation and restore; no worker or successfully published envelope survives the closed scope.
4. Race duplicate resume, mutation and stale close events; preserve the single queue and R10 takeover behavior.
5. Fail journal persistence and worker startup separately; return failure, retain recoverable input and release resources.

**Verification:** U1's baseline and all existing runtime backends pass against the refactored service; real fixture workers exit without leaked handles.

### U4. Build managed discovery and authenticated presence

content.text:
Source-to-element (S7) passed its full sign-off at `648bdc39` and is merged into the controller branch, together with its `elements` MCP tool. The merged tree differs from the signed-off one only by the plan document.

**What's merged so far**

| Slice | What it is |
|---|---|
| S0 | The plan |
| S1 / S1b | Vite+ tooling and the dependency update |
| S2 | Lint checks against a recorded baseline that can only shrink |
| S3 | One install for all of CIVIC |
| S4 | The shared state-machine core and the work-request lifecycle |
| S5 | The MCP server on Effect |
| S6 | CIVIC as a project in its own picker |
| S7 | Source-to-element |
| S9 | The preview lifecycle |
| S9b | The cleanup helper for old preview builds |

**Running now**
- [S8 lint cleanup](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A16209525-2cb7-42a2-8644-ba7b626bdb62): the last 23 lint findings before backend coverage can be signed off.
- [S10 U1-U2 run journal tests and lifecycle machines](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A06c9b3d0-a7ce-47c7-b95b-7a786afc6dca): the first two of the app server's six units.
  - First it writes tests that lock in how recorded runs recover today.
  - Then it adds the app server and run state machines, with their timers tested on a test clock rather than real waits.
  - It doesn't wire them in yet.
  - One constraint I set: outside apps install the canvas package from git, so the new server-only dependencies must not become requirements for those apps.

**Next, once S8 merges**
- The agent-tool integrations (S11).
- The CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off tools (S11b): open a review for a worktree, link a request to a work item, read coverage.
- Checking the possible checkbox-replay mismatch the S8 worker found.

Bounded implementation worker for CIVIC (this checkout). Slice S11 "Harness integrations" of docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md (read §1 harness row, §6 S11, AGENTS.md, docs/decisions/0006 (CIVIC makes no model calls and launches no agents), 0007, 0022). Today: integrations/claude-code (Claude Code plugin: skills, hooks, bin/civic-mcp launcher, bin/civic-home, bin/session-start), integrations/claude-code/codex.mcp.json, root .claude-plugin/marketplace.json; the MCP server is review/src/mcp.ts (one Effect Schema tool table — TOOLS; do not edit its tools).

Goal: CIVIC is usable from any agent harness through the SAME stdio MCP server, with thin per-harness wrappers that only point at it — no per-harness tool lists anywhere (the server lists its own tools).
1. One launcher contract: `integrations/claude-code/bin/civic-mcp` (or a harness-neutral `bin/civic-mcp` it delegates to — choose the smallest) finds CIVIC's checkout (CIVIC_HOME) and starts the server. Harness configs reference only this launcher.
2. Config for each harness CIVIC documents, DERIVED from one small source (a single JSON/TS description of "command + args + env" rendered into each harness's config format by a function, with a test that every rendered config points at the same launcher): Claude Code (plugin, exists), Codex (codex.mcp.json / config.toml snippet), OpenCode (opencode.json `mcp` entry), Cursor (.cursor/mcp.json), and ACP agents (an ACP client passes `mcpServers` in `session/new` — document the stdio server entry; e.g. Amp, Gemini CLI via ACP). Do not write into the user's real harness config files; `civic integrate <harness>` (wired into review/src/cli.ts the way other commands are) PRINTS the snippet for that harness, and README explains where it goes. Lean on harness-native features (plugins/skills where the harness has them) but keep skills text harness-neutral.
3. Behaviour tests before any real agent (a "misbehaving agent" suite, real server process, temp git repo store, no mocks): drive the server exactly as a harness would over stdio (initialize → tools/list → calls) and assert refusals: a write with a stale `@version` is refused naming the change; claiming a request another agent holds is refused naming the holder; an agent cannot resolve (no resolve tool exists; any attempt via unknown tool name fails); report_fix without a claim is refused; oversized/invalid input is rejected naming the field. Also a smoke test per rendered config: spawn the launcher exactly as the config says (command/args/env) and complete initialize + tools/list.
4. New code lint-clean: `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs` must pass (shrink-only; CIVIC house style is fine).

Rules: never change HOME (set CIVIC_HOME/temp dirs via env in tests only); temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC, any .civic-canvas folder, or any real harness config (~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.config/opencode, ~/.cursor); installs only inside this worktree (`pnpm --dir packages install --frozen-lockfile`); no new dependencies; no model calls. Load gate before any test suite: `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/REDACTED/8f3b2eca-0508-4f5d-8344-d9ed70c2da42/scratchpad/gate.sh`; ≤2 test workers. Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments; README text in everyday words.

Verify: `pnpm --dir packages run check`, the new behaviour and smoke tests, `pnpm --dir packages --filter @civic/review test` after the gate. Report only: diff summary, the single source and the harnesses rendered, what each misbehaving-agent test asserts, commands with pass/fail, blockers.

content.text:
Mostly because of your landing rule, plus caution after today's failures. Batching would be cheaper here, and I'd switch to it.

**Why I've been queuing:**
- **Your rule.** "Every change passes its own checks and full suites before landing; land each verified slice immediately; never batch unrelated work." I read that as one sign-off per slice, on that slice's exact commit.
- **Load.** I only run one heavy job at a time, and only when load is below 6. Each sign-off takes about 4–5 minutes of machine time, but the waiting for a quiet machine is far longer. Orca's test runs have kept load at 8–20 for much of the evening.
- **Telling failures apart.** Several runs today failed, and I could see which slice caused each one. In a combined run I'd have to work that out afterwards.

**Why batching makes sense now:**
- S8, S10 and S11 don't touch the same code. One sign-off on the top of a stack of all three checks the exact tree that lands: one wait for a quiet machine instead of three, and about 10 minutes less heavy CPU.
- Batching the *check* isn't batching the *work*. Each slice still lands as its own commit and merge, so history stays per slice.
- If the combined run fails, the log says which test failed, and that almost always points to one slice. I'd fix that slice or drop it from the stack, then re-run. In the worst case it costs one extra run.

**What you'd give up:** the trees in between, for example S8 alone without S10 on top, would never be signed off themselves. Only the final stacked tree would be. Since each merge lands straight on the next, nothing ever sits on the branch in a state that wasn't checked.

**Decision for you:** I'd switch to stacking S8, S10 and S11 now, with one sign-off for the three, and keep batching like this going forward. If you'd rather keep strict one-slice-one-sign-off, I'll carry on queuing. Shall I switch?

- [Architecture decisions](docs/decisions). The first demo uses [Microsoft Fluent 2](docs/decisions/0001-fluent-2-demo-design-system.md).
-- The [review loop](review/README.md), the [canvas](packages/canvas/README.md), and the [Claude Code and Codex plugin](integrations/claude-code/README.md).

+- The [review loop](review/README.md), the [canvas](packages/canvas/README.md), and [agent harness setup](integrations/claude-code/README.md) for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and ACP clients (`civic integrate <harness>`).
-# CIVIC for Claude Code and Codex
A thin plugin for [decision 0007](../../docs/decisions/0007-review-to-agent-loop.md)'s review to agent loop. All logic lives in CIVIC's [`review/`](../../review) package. The plugin provides:

-- **The `civic` MCP server** (`review/src/mcp.ts`). It offers `list_requests`, `get_request` (which returns the frozen captures as images), `claim`, `release`, `comment`, `repro`, `report_fix`, `add_check`, `register_pr`, `annotate`, `context` and `gaps`. Agents can't resolve requests, accept checks or change a lane (D35). `report_fix` with a preview runs CIVIC's own re-capture, which is written as `actor:civic`.
-- **A skill**, `work-a-request`, that walks Claude through choosing a request, claiming it, reading it, reproducing it, fixing it, committing, and reporting the fix.
+- **The `civic` MCP server** (`review/src/mcp.ts`). The server lists its own tools. Agents can't resolve requests, accept checks or change a lane (D35).
+- **A skill**, `work-a-request`, that walks an agent through choosing a request, claiming it, reading it, reproducing it, fixing it, committing, and reporting the fix.
- **Commands**: `/civic:next` picks up the oldest unclaimed request, and `/civic:request <id>` works one request.
- **A SessionStart hook** that lists open requests, so Claude can offer to pick one up.
- **Commands become skills.** Codex turns `/civic:next` into the `civic:source-command-next` skill and leaves out `/civic:request`. Ask for the `civic:work-a-request` skill with a request ID instead.

input.task:
Bounded implementation worker for CIVIC (this checkout). Slice S11b of docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md — read §5b "CIVIC and Orca, both ways" in full (shared shapes WorkRef/ScreenRef/Shot/ChangedScreens/ReviewSession/Coverage, the MCP surface table, the three flows), plus AGENTS.md and docs/decisions/0006 (no model calls, launches no agents), 0007 (D35 narrow agent write path), 0021 (civic preview), 0022. CIVIC stays generic: no Orca types or names in code (`system` in WorkRef is opaque). Orca is read-only for you; do not touch it.

Build the CIVIC side:
1. `links: WorkRef[]` on work requests and a `workRef` on annotations made in a review session (graph schema + validation in graph/src, following its conventions; an annotation's workRef becomes its request's first link).
2. MCP tools as rows in review/src/mcp.ts's Effect Schema TOOLS table (one row each; JSON Schemas are derived automatically): `changed_screens` (cwd, base → ChangedScreens, using review/src/elements.ts `diffRanges` + `elements` over the tagged captures CIVIC already keeps, plus journeys through those screens; report limits in `limits[]` when no capture covers a changed file), `open_review` (cwd, workRef, optional screens, optional shots default 1440 & 390 × light & dark → ReviewSession; it starts or attaches that worktree's `civic preview` through review/src/preview — no new launcher; no records written), `close_review` (stops only what that session started, via the preview's recorded processes), `link_request` (request id@version + workRef → adds one link, version-checked, nothing else), `list_requests` gains an optional workRef filter, and `coverage` (cwd or project → the plan's Coverage shape: screens, journeys, and `backend` from the existing `readBackendCoverage` in review/src/backend.ts — reuse, don't duplicate the existing `backend_coverage` row's logic).
3. MCP resources: `civic://requests?system=…&id=…` and `civic://coverage/{project}`, with `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `resources/subscribe` and `notifications/resources/updated` when the underlying records change (watch the store's files with bounded, cleaned-up watchers owned by an Effect scope — no polling loops, no raw timers). Advertise the `resources` capability.
4. Permissions: D35 unchanged — no tool resolves a request, accepts a check, or annotates on the owner's behalf; open_review/link_request write no review outcome.
5. Tests (real processes, temp git repo store, no mocks): a coordinator test that plays Orca over stdio against the real server: open_review on a temp worktree → an owner annotation through the overlay/API with that session's workRef → `civic://requests` notification arrives and lists it under the work item → link_request on another request → list_requests filtered by workRef → coverage includes backend → close_review leaves no processes. Plus refusal tests (stale version on link_request; close_review on someone else's session).
6. Write `docs/integrations/orca-proposal.md`: the Orca-side wiring proposal from §5b (for the Orca controller; everyday words; no Orca code).
7. New code lint-clean: `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs` must pass (shrink-only; CIVIC house style is fine).

Rules: never change HOME; temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC, the running 3012 instance, any .civic-canvas folder, or /Users/taymoor/Projects/orca; installs only inside this worktree (`pnpm --dir packages install --frozen-lockfile`); no new dependencies. Another worker is changing packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.mjs — do not edit it. Load gate before any test suite: `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/REDACTED/8f3b2eca-0508-4f5d-8344-d9ed70c2da42/scratchpad/gate.sh`; ≤2 test workers. Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments.

Verify: `pnpm --dir packages run check`, your new tests (after the gate). Do not run the full suites; the controller's batch sign-off does. Report only: diff summary, tools/resources added, how notifications are driven, commands with pass/fail, blockers.

content.text:
Three more slices are merged onto the controller branch: backend coverage (S8), the first two app-server units (S10 U1–U2) and the agent-tool integrations (S11). They passed one combined sign-off at `8375aea2`, and the controller branch now points at exactly that commit.

| Merged | What it is |
|---|---|
| S0 | The plan |
| S1, S1b | Vite+ tooling and the dependency update |
| S2 | Lint checks against a baseline that can only shrink |
| S3 | One install for all of CIVIC |
| S4 | The shared state-machine core and the work-request lifecycle |
| S5 | The MCP server on Effect |
| S6 | CIVIC as a project in its own picker |
| S7 | Source-to-element |
| S8 | Backend coverage |
| S9, S9b | The preview lifecycle, and the cleanup helper for old preview builds |
| S10 U1–U2 | Run-recovery tests, and the app server and run state machines |
| S11 | The agent-tool integrations |

Two workers are running now, on separate files:
- [S11b coordinator hand-off tools](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A00f79df4-fc86-41d6-a8eb-04f529996741): the CIVIC side of the hand-off with Orca.
  - It can work out which screens a change touches, open and close a review of a worktree, link a request to an outside work item, and give one combined coverage report.
  - A coordinator such as Orca gets a notification when new comments arrive, instead of having to keep asking.
  - It also writes the proposal for how Orca would wire this in. No Orca code changes; CIVIC never calls Orca.
- [S10 U3 supervise the run service](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A0539a94a-7bac-41cd-b0dc-891d5b6f0c8c): wires the run machine into the live run service.
  - Effect takes over the workers, timeouts and shutdown.
  - The run service's existing limits and journals stay as they are.
  - Outside apps can still install the canvas package from git.

When both are back, they get one combined sign-off.

Still to do after those: the rest of the app server and the desktop window (S10 U4–U6), the cleanup pass (S12), and checking the possible checkbox-replay mismatch the S8 worker reported.

I'm treating the partial work as having two real gaps: tagged captures aren't persisted, which the changed-screens logic depends on, and preview sessions have no path to attach a workRef. My plan is to land the links, link_request, and filter pieces now as S11b part 1, once they're verified, and push the capture persistence and preview context work into a follow-up.

I'm laying out the follow-up worker's tasks: persisting tagged captures, wiring workRef into preview sessions, resources and notifications, the coverage tool, and open/close_review. For the capture persistence, I'm weighing two options: save tagged captures at capture time, or compute them on demand from a running preview with a bounded cache keyed by source revision. I'm leaning toward the on-demand approach, since open_review already starts a preview.

I'm planning to commit the partial work now as part 1, putting it on a branch and temporarily switching the main worktree to that branch so the follow-up worker starts from it.

Bounded implementation worker for CIVIC (this checkout). Finish slice S11b of docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md §5b (read it all: shapes, MCP surface table, three flows). HEAD's commit "feat: Link work requests to an outside coordinator's work items" already added WorkRef on graph records, request links, `link_request`, and the `list_requests` workRef filter, with tests in review/test/work-links.test.ts — build on it, don't redo it. Read AGENTS.md and docs/decisions/0006, 0007, 0009, 0021, 0022. CIVIC stays generic (WorkRef.system is opaque); never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/orca.

The previous worker stopped at two gaps; here is the design to use:
A. **Tagged captures for `changed_screens`.** Don't invent a parallel store. When CIVIC renders a scenario in a browser for review or recapture, it can read the page's `data-civic-source` tags with review/src/elements.ts `taggedCapture(page, scenario)`. Persist those per project and source fingerprint (the same content identity CIVIC already binds captures to) in the review store, bounded (one file per scenario, replaced when the source fingerprint changes), and expose a reader. `changed_screens(cwd, base)` = `diffRanges(git diff base...HEAD)` → `elements()` over the stored tagged captures for the current source, plus the journeys whose scenarios include those screens (from the project's scenario registry); any changed file under the project's sources that no stored capture renders goes into `limits[]` in everyday words. If no tagged capture exists yet for the current source, `open_review` (below) collects them once from its running preview with Playwright (bounded: one page, sequential scenarios, closed afterwards) — reuse how recapture launches browsers.
B. **Session context.** `open_review(cwd, workRef, screens?, shots?)` starts or attaches that worktree's `civic preview` (review/src/preview — reuse; add an option rather than a new launcher) and records the session (id, workRef, which processes it started) in the preview registry. Annotations saved through that preview's review proxy are stamped with the session's workRef SERVER-SIDE by the proxy/overlay server (it knows which preview it fronts) — never trust a client-sent workRef. `close_review(id)` stops only processes that session started (recorded pid + start time, as civic preview stop does); a different session's id is refused.
C. `coverage(cwd|project)` → the plan's Coverage shape (screens, journeys, and `backend` from the existing `readBackendCoverage` in review/src/backend.ts — reuse the `backend_coverage` row's logic, don't duplicate it).
D. **Resources:** `civic://requests?system=…&id=…` and `civic://coverage/{project}` with `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `resources/subscribe`/`unsubscribe`, and `notifications/resources/updated` when the underlying store files change — driven by `fs.watch` on the store's record file(s), owned by an Effect scope (one watcher per subscribed resource, closed on unsubscribe and on stdin end), debounced with Effect Schedule, no polling, no raw timers. Advertise the `resources` capability in initialize.
All new tools are rows in review/src/mcp.ts's Effect Schema TOOLS table. D35 unchanged: nothing resolves, accepts checks, or annotates for the owner.

Tests (real processes, temp git repo, synthetic example such as packages/canvas/examples/notebook, no mocks): a coordinator test over stdio against the real server: subscribe to `civic://requests?system=test&id=W1` → open_review for a temp worktree with workRef W1 → save an annotation through that preview's API → a resources/updated notification arrives and resources/read lists the request under W1 → changed_screens after editing one example source file names its screen → coverage returns screens/journeys/backend → close_review leaves none of its processes running and refuses another session's id. Docs: update docs/integrations/orca-proposal.md if anything changed. New code lint-clean: `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs` must pass.

Rules: never change HOME; temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC, the running 3012 instance, or any .civic-canvas folder; installs only inside this worktree (`pnpm --dir packages install --frozen-lockfile`); no new dependencies. Another worker is changing packages/canvas/server/runtime-service.mjs — don't edit it. Load gate before any test suite or browser run: `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/REDACTED/8f3b2eca-0508-4f5d-8344-d9ed70c2da42/scratchpad/gate.sh`; ≤2 test workers. Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments. Do not run the full suites (the controller's batch sign-off does).

Report only: diff summary, where tagged captures are stored and their identity, how the session workRef is stamped, how notifications are driven, commands with pass/fail, blockers.

customTitle: CIVIC: Effect + XState rebuild, MCP, self-review features

content.text:
The CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off (S11b) is about half done, and none of it is merged yet. The working half is committed on its own branch, and a second worker is building the rest from a design I set.

**Committed (`190c7322`):**
- Work requests can be linked to a coordinator's work items. Orca is the first coordinator, but CIVIC stores only an opaque system name and id, so no Orca details live in CIVIC.
- A comment made for a work item passes that link to the request it becomes.
- `link_request` adds a link and refuses if the request changed since it was read. `list_requests` can show just one work item's requests.
- The Orca-side wiring proposal is written up in `docs/integrations/orca-proposal.md`.
- Type checks, the lint baseline and the new link tests pass.

**Why the first worker stopped:** two pieces of the design were missing.
- To answer "which screens does this change touch", CIVIC needs a saved record of which elements each screen draws. Nothing saved one.
- A running preview had no way to know which work item a review was for, so comments couldn't carry the link.

**The design I gave the second worker,** [S11b part 2 review sessions, changed screens, resources](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3Aea6b19ca-0dda-41e4-b9b5-c609ca8094b4):
- **Element records:** when CIVIC draws a screen in a browser, it saves that screen's element locations for the current version of the code, one file per screen, replaced when the code changes. If none exist yet, opening a review collects them once from the preview it starts.
- **Review sessions:** `open_review` starts or reuses that worktree's preview and remembers which work item the review is for. The preview's own server then stamps that link on every comment. It never trusts a link sent by the browser.
- **Closing:** `close_review` stops only the processes its own session started, and refuses another session's id.
- **Coverage:** one combined report of screens, journeys and backend, reusing the existing backend logic rather than writing it again.
- **Notifications:** a coordinator subscribes to a work item's requests or a project's coverage. It's told when the underlying records change, using file watching that is cleaned up when it unsubscribes. No repeated checking, no raw timers.
- **Test:** one end-to-end check plays Orca against the real server. It subscribes, opens a review, sees a comment arrive, asks which screens a change touched, reads coverage and closes the review.

The worker wiring the run machines into the run service (S10 U3) is still running. When both are back, the whole hand-off and U3 get one combined sign-off.

content.content:
3:.civic-canvas/
10:.civic/*
11:!.civic/civic.json
11:Decision 0007 (D39) put local review records in the git common directory, `<repo>/.git/civic/`, so every worktree sees the same annotations and nothing is committed to a product branch. To review a connected app, CIVIC therefore wrote into that app's `.git`. The owner does not want CIVIC, or anything else that isn't git, writing there. The records are also evidence, so they can't live in a cache. Vite keeps its own cache under `node_modules`, which an install or a clean wipes, so that was considered and rejected.
16:2. **The folder hides itself from git.** CIVIC writes `.civic/.gitignore` containing `*` and `!civic.json` when it first uses the folder, so records and captures can't be staged by `git add -A`, and `civic.json` can. A repository may also add `.civic/*` and `!.civic/civic.json` to its own `.gitignore`; CIVIC never edits a connected app's tracked files. It asks git (`git check-ignore`) before its first write, and stops if the records would not be ignored.
17:3. **A working tree can come from another branch, so the store distrusts tracked files.** Checking out a branch could supply `.civic/records.graph.json`, or a `preview-auth.json` that names a file to send as a sign-in key. The store refuses every read and write while git tracks anything in `.civic/` but `civic.json`, and says how to untrack it. The git common directory could not be checked out, so D39 never needed this. A link or file someone plants in the folder locally is not defended against: whoever can write the working tree could always write `.git/civic/` too.

Newer rules from docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md §2 and docs/decisions/0022 win. U1–U3 are merged: packages/canvas/server/server-lifecycle.ts (server machine) and run-lifecycle.ts; runtime-service.mjs runs each run under the run machine and an Effect scope; `ws` is the plan's socket library — check whether it is already installed in the packages workspace; add it (and @types/ws) to @civic/canvas runtime/dev deps only if not, with exact versions from the plan or current caret.

Constraints: Effect and XState are runtime dependencies of @civic/canvas; do NOT import @civic/core at runtime (outside apps install canvas from git — packages/install.check.mjs). Loopback only; keep existing origin/authentication/project-binding checks (packages/shell/server/review-server.mjs). Never put tickets or capabilities in URLs or logs. customTitle: CIVIC: Effect + XState rebuild, MCP, self-review features

content.text:
The CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off (S11b) and wiring the run machine into the run service (S10 U3) are combined on one candidate branch, and their one sign-off is running now. Nothing new has landed yet.

**What the hand-off adds:**
- A coordinator such as Orca can open a review of a worktree for one of its work items. The preview's own server stamps that work item on every comment and ignores any link the browser sends.
- `close_review` stops only what its own session started.
- `changed_screens` turns a diff into the screens it touches. It uses element records CIVIC saves for each screen and each version of the code, in `.civic/`. Git ignores that folder apart from `civic.json`, which is where decision 0020 puts captures.
- A coordinator can subscribe to a work item's requests or to a project's coverage, and is told when they change.

**Tests so far:**
- 16 focused tests pass.
- The end-to-end check that plays Orca against the real server passed before the worker's last small additions. The sign-off running now covers those additions too.

**One known limit,** written into the Orca proposal: if a run is replayed only inside a preview, the coverage report shows it when read, but no change notice is sent yet. A coordinator can read the coverage report again to catch it.

**Started:** [S10 U4 managed discovery and presence](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A12a89832-c02f-444b-b3a8-bc5ba3e8586d).
- When a CIVIC server starts, it registers itself. Two servers racing for one store end with one owner.
- A port already held by another program is refused, never killed.
- A leftover registration is taken over only with proof that its owner is dead.
- Browser tabs and the desktop app get single-use, short-lived passes to connect. Those passes never appear in URLs or logs.
- Wiring in the desktop window and the browser comes in the next unit, U5.

content.text:
The automated security review found a real problem in the new CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off code, and I've fixed it. Nothing from this batch has landed yet.

**The problem:** `changed_screens` takes a diff base from the agent and passed it straight into `git diff`. A base such as `--output=<file>` starts with a dash, so git would read it as an option and write that file.

**The fix:** CIVIC now turns the base into a commit SHA before using it, with `rev-parse --end-of-options`. It refuses anything that isn't a real commit, and only that SHA reaches `git diff`. A new test checks that `--output=…`, `-p`, an unknown name and an empty value are all refused and that no file gets written. It passes, and so do the type check and the lint baseline.

**Not changed:** the reviewer also suggested limiting which folder an agent can point CIVIC at. I left that alone. Every CIVIC tool already takes the agent's own checkout as its working folder, and the agent already runs on this machine with its own file access, so a limit there wouldn't protect anything.

**Sign-off:** the sign-off that had started was testing the unfixed code, so I stopped it. The fix is now its own commit in the batch with the rest of the hand-off (S11b) and U3, the step that runs each run under its state machine. One combined sign-off for all of it is running now.

The worker on server discovery and connection passes (S10 U4) is still running.

content.text:
The worker for server discovery and connection passes (S10 U4) stopped partway, and I've saved its work as an untested work-in-progress commit on its own branch, `feat/managed-host` (`bfec8273`).

**Why it stopped:** my brief told it the previous step (U3, running each run under its state machine) was already merged. It isn't yet; U3 is in the batch now being signed off. The worker started from a version without U3 and correctly stopped when the code didn't match. The mistake was in my brief, not its work.

**What it built:**
- A server registration in a private folder. A lock makes sure only one CIVIC server owns a store. A leftover registration is taken over only when the system reports its owner process is gone.
- One control connection that browser tabs and the desktop app use to stay attached:
  - browser tabs get a single-use pass that expires after 10 seconds;
  - the desktop app uses its own private key;
  - messages over 16 KB are refused, and a backed-up queue disconnects the client so it reloads.
- Vite now runs behind one stable server, so restarting Vite doesn't drop those connections.

**Not done yet:**
- None of U4's tests have run.
- Its package changes overlap with U3's, since both make Effect and XState real dependencies of the canvas.

**Next:**
1. The batch sign-off finishes: the CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off, U3, and the security fix.
2. I merge U4 on top, which will likely need a small conflict fix in `package.json`.
3. A worker finishes U4's tests against the real run service.

The batch sign-off failed again at its last step, so the hand-off work and the run-service wiring still haven't landed. The fix is in and that step now passes on its own; the full sign-off is running again.

Wiring the run machine into the run service (U3) made the server load a TypeScript file, `run-lifecycle.ts`. Node refuses to strip TypeScript inside an installed package, so an app that installed the canvas from git couldn't start its server.

**The fix:** the run machine is now plain JavaScript (`run-lifecycle.mjs`), with a small type file for the tests. Its tests pass, and the type check and lint baseline are clean. I ran the install check alone on the new batch head, and the empty app opened the Notebook example with 4 screens.

**For the next step:** the app-server machine (`server-lifecycle.ts`) will hit the same problem when U4 starts loading it, so it gets the same treatment then.

If the sign-off passes, three things land together:
- the CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off;
- the run-service wiring;
- the earlier security fix for `changed_screens`.

Bounded investigation-and-fix worker for CIVIC (this checkout). An earlier worker reported, while building backend coverage, "checkbox replay has a confirmed discovery-state mismatch": recording a live run that toggles a checkbox and then replaying the tape diverges, apparently because the recorded step's expected screen state (fields / discovery state) for a checkbox doesn't match what replay observes. Recording and replay live in packages/canvas/src/runtime-bridge.ts, runtime-session.ts, replay code under packages/canvas/src (see replay.test.ts), packages/shell/server/review-recording.mjs; the examples with checkboxes are probably packages/canvas/examples/tasks or team-board (grep for type="checkbox"); browser checks for record/replay are in packages/canvas/server/canvas-host.check.mjs. Read AGENTS.md and docs/decisions/0009, 0017 (journey steps declare expected state).

1. Reproduce it with a real browser on a synthetic example (add a failing check first; reuse the existing record/replay check pattern). If you cannot reproduce it, say so with what you tried and stop — do not invent a fix.
2. Find the root cause and fix it once in the shared code (not per example), keeping the replay's strictness: a real divergence must still stop with "Replay diverged at step N".
3. The new check passes; existing replay/runtime-bridge tests still pass.
New code lint-clean: `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs` must pass (shrink-only).

The batch passed its sign-off at `62739c80`, and the controller branch is moved forward to exactly that commit. Three things landed together:
- **The CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off (S11b).**
  - Requests can be linked to a coordinator's work items.
  - A coordinator can open and close a review of a worktree, and ask which screens a change touches.
  - It can read one combined coverage report.
  - It is notified when new comments arrive.
- **The security fix** for the diff base an agent passes in.
- **U3:** each recorded run now runs under its state machine, with Effect handling workers, timeouts and shutdown. The run machine is plain JavaScript, so apps that install the canvas from git can still start it.

**U4 (server discovery and connection passes) is back with a worker, finishing on top of U3.** U4's own changes are now merged with everything that landed, with one small dependency conflict fixed. It passes the type check and the lint baseline. The worker is:
- connecting it to the real run service;
- converting the app-server machine to plain JavaScript, the same fix as the run machine;
- running its tests with real servers and sockets: two servers racing, a foreign port refused, takeover only when the old owner is gone, single-use passes, size limits, and no secrets in URLs or logs;
- running the install-from-git check.

content.text:
U4 (server discovery and shared connections) is committed as one change on top of the controller branch (`caba48e4`), but not merged yet. The install check passes on that commit: an empty app installs CIVIC from git and opens the Notebook example with 4 screens.

What U4 does:
- **One server per store.** A CIVIC server registers itself in a private folder in the store and takes a lock.
  - A second server for the same store hands over to the first.
  - A program already holding the port is refused and left running.
  - A leftover registration is taken over only once its owner process is gone.
- **Staying attached.** Browser tabs and the desktop app stay connected through one local control channel. Tabs use passes that work once and expire after 10 seconds; the desktop app uses a private key. Neither ever appears in URLs or logs.
- **Restarts.** The server's Effect scope keeps the run services alive across Vite restarts, and its state machine moves through ready, attached, lost, stopping, drained and closed.

Its focused tests pass: 36 node tests and 6 lifecycle tests, with real servers and sockets. The lint baseline is unchanged.

Not tested: restarting Vite while the desktop app is connected. That belongs with U5, which attaches the desktop window.

Per the batching rule, U4 waits for the checkbox-replay worker. If that comes back with a fix, both get one combined sign-off; if not, U4 is signed off alone.

Bounded implementation worker for CIVIC (this checkout). S10 unit U5 "Attach browser and minimal Electron clients" of docs/plans/2026-10-18-0515-feat-effect-app-server-lifecycle-plan.md (read R1–R6, R11, R14, AE1–AE3, AE6, AE8, KTD4, KTD8 and U5). Newer rules in docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md §2 (electron ^45.3.2 as a devDependency of packages/local; Electron main as an Effect program) and docs/decisions/0022 win. HEAD includes U4: the managed host (registration, owner lock, control socket at /api/civic/control, single-use browser tickets via the `civic-control,<ticket>` subprotocol, desktop bearer capability, server machine) — read `git log -3` and the managed-host files under packages/canvas/server/. Today's Electron shell is packages/local/desktop.mjs (+ desktop-*.mjs, desktop-launch.mjs needs CIVIC_ELECTRON_BINARY), and its checks are packages/local/*.electron.mjs (run by `test:electron`).

Goal:
1. Browser: each top-level CIVIC tab (not preview frames, not capture browsers) gets a ticket through the existing authenticated review middleware and keeps one presence connection, reconnecting within the grace window after reload; hidden tabs stay attached.
2. Electron: main holds one desktop connection until actual Quit (closing the last window keeps it); a renderer crash doesn't release it. Electron main discovers/starts the managed host for the store (via U4's discovery) instead of assuming a fixed origin; the window title shows the worktree's branch (docs/self-dogfood.md follow-up 1) and each worktree gets its own Electron profile. Electron main's lifetimes are an Effect program (scoped windows/listeners/connection); add `electron` ^45.3.2 to packages/local devDependencies (allowBuilds already permits it? check packages/pnpm-workspace.yaml), so `test:electron` no longer needs CIVIC_ELECTRON_BINARY (keep the variable as an override).
3. Tests (real processes, Playwright `_electron` like the existing *.electron.mjs, temp store, ephemeral ports): AE1 (Electron quits, browser and its run continue), AE2 (last window closes → server kept; Quit → released), AE3 (tab reload within grace → same server instance), AE8 (all clients gone → host exits; launcher dies before attach → no orphan). Keep every existing packages/local check passing.
Anything loaded at runtime from @civic/canvas must stay plain JavaScript (outside apps install it from git; Node doesn't strip types under node_modules). No raw timers; `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs` must pass.

Rules: never change HOME; temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC, the running 3012 instance, or any .civic-canvas folder; no real user Electron profile; installs only inside this worktree (`pnpm --dir packages install`). Load gate before any test suite or Electron run: `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/REDACTED/8f3b2eca-0508-4f5d-8344-d9ed70c2da42/scratchpad/gate.sh`; ≤2 test workers; one Electron instance at a time. Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments; owner-facing text in everyday words. Do not run the full suites.

Report only: diff summary, how tabs and Electron attach, commands with pass/fail (including which AE scenarios ran), blockers.

content.text:
The checkbox replay bug is real, and it's fixed and committed. It's in a batch with U4 (one shared server per store), merged with no conflicts. That batch's single sign-off is waiting for a quiet machine; nothing from it has landed yet.

**What was wrong:** on the Tasks example, ticking "Water the plants", saving the run and replaying it stopped at step 5. Two bugs in the shared recording and replay code caused it:
- **Recording saved the wrong "before" state.** It read the screen after the browser had already ticked the box, so the run expected "ticked" before the step happened.
- **Replay hid the tick from the app.** It swallowed the change event it generated, so the app never saw the tick and never sent its update to its server.

**The fix:**
- The starting state is now recorded before the click.
- Replay passes its change events through to the app.
- Clicking a checkbox's label is recorded once, not twice.

**Checks:**
- A new browser check fails before the fix and passes after. It covers a direct click, a label click and the Space key.
- The 13 recording and replay tests pass, including the one that checks a real mismatch still stops the replay.

**Decision for you:** runs recorded with the old behaviour that tick a checkbox will now fail to replay, because they saved the wrong starting state. They need to be recorded again. I haven't touched any saved runs in your stores. Tell me whether you want them found and listed for you.

**Started meanwhile:** U5, which attaches the browser tabs and the desktop app to the shared server, in [S10 U5 attach browser and Electron](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A6ef696b2-eaa1-43d4-ad26-012161c19b57). It starts from the batch so it can build on U4. It covers:
- each top-level browser tab keeps one connection and gets it back after a reload;
- the desktop app finds or starts the server for its store, keeps it running until you actually quit, shows the branch in its window title, and uses its own profile for each worktree;

content.text:
Server discovery and shared connections (S10 U4) and the checkbox replay fix passed one combined sign-off and are merged. The controller branch is now exactly the signed-off commit, `8aed9b23`.

**Merged so far:**
- The foundations: Vite+ tooling, every dependency updated, lint checks that can only shrink, one install for all of CIVIC, the shared state-machine core, and the MCP server on Effect.
- **Source-to-element:** pick an element and get the file and line that drew it. It works first on CIVIC's own screens, which now appear in its own picker.
- **Backend coverage:** which server routes and functions each journey reaches, and which none do.
- **Agent tools:** one MCP server that every agent tool connects to, tested against a badly behaved agent.
- **The CIVIC ⇄ Orca hand-off:** work-item links, review sessions, changed screens, and notifications.
- **The app server:** run-recovery tests, the state machines, runs managed by Effect, and one shared server per store (U1–U4). The preview lifecycle and the cleanup helper for old preview builds are in too.
- **The checkbox replay fix.**

**Running now:**
- [S10 U5 attach browser and Electron](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A6ef696b2-eaa1-43d4-ad26-012161c19b57): browser tabs and the desktop app join the shared server.
- [S12 cleanup layering violations](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3Afe28cb07-8a54-4f37-a810-5f1de5b22f52): the first cleanup pass.
  - It goes through the 11 places where the graph or importers reach for Effect, XState or process code, and the 7 where browser code imports server code. Each one gets moved, or the checker gets corrected if it's a false alarm.
  - It also tightens review's import rule so that imports written with a computed path can't slip past it.

**Left after these:** U6, the final install and recovery checks for the app server.

**Still waiting on you:** saved runs recorded before the checkbox fix that tick a checkbox need recording again. Do you want me to find and list them for you?

That error box came from the U5 worker's desktop-app test, not from your CIVIC. The test runs in its own temporary checkout (`t3-86fd78ba…`), so your live instance and stores were untouched. You can click OK.

The test found a real bug. When a page in the desktop app updates its title, the app renames the window. If the window has already closed by then, the rename throws, and Electron shows that error box. The same code is on your main checkout, so you could hit it there too, not just in tests.

I've redirected the worker, mid-run, to:
1. **Fix it at the source.** Every late event in the desktop app's main process checks the window still exists before touching it. A new test closes a window while a title update is in flight.
2. **Keep error boxes off your screen during tests.** Under test, an uncaught error is logged and fails the test instead of opening a native box.
3. **Leave nothing running.** Any Electron it started is stopped when the run ends.

It then carries on with the rest of U5. U5 and the cleanup pass (S12) will be signed off together once it's back.

content.text:
U5, which attaches the browser tabs and the desktop app to the shared server, is finished and committed. It's batched with the first cleanup pass (S12), and their combined sign-off is queued until the machine is quiet. Neither has landed yet.

**What U5 does:**
- Each top-level CIVIC browser tab keeps one connection to the shared server, even while hidden. Preview frames and the desktop app's own views don't count as tabs.
- The desktop app finds or starts the server for its store and keeps it running until you actually quit; closing the last window doesn't stop it. Each worktree gets its own desktop profile, and the branch name shows in the window title.
- Electron now installs with CIVIC, so the desktop tests no longer need you to point them at an Electron binary.

**The error box you saw:** the desktop app tried to rename a window that had already closed, which is what threw that error box. Late events from a closed window are now ignored. Under test, uncaught errors go to the test log instead of a box on your screen. The worker also found no leftover Electron or server processes from its runs.

**Desktop tests that passed:**
- Quitting the desktop app leaves the browser and its run going.
- Closing the last window keeps the server; quitting releases it.
- Reloading a tab within the grace window reconnects to the same server.
- Once every client is gone, the server shuts down cleanly. If the launcher dies before anything attaches, nothing is left running.
- Renderer and main-process crashes, and late title or resize events after a window closes.

**Not exercised:** whether hidden tabs and preview frames are kept off the connection list was checked by reading the code, not by a separate test.

The standard sign-off doesn't run the desktop tests, so I added them to this batch's run, on the same tree.

The last app-server unit, U6 (final install and recovery checks), starts after this batch lands.

The browser tabs and the desktop app now attach to the shared server (S10 U5), and the first cleanup pass (S12) is in. Both are merged on the controller branch after one combined check: the full sign-off at `050fc5d5` plus all three desktop test files. The controller branch is now exactly that commit, and no Electron processes were left running.

Everything in the plan has now landed except the last app-server unit, U6, which a worker has just started: [S10 U6 install, recovery and delivery checks](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A13ff8f7e-2c19-4ff5-9bd9-6a05142c8170). It does three things:
- **Install test.** An empty app installs CIVIC from git, starts the shared server, and attaches one browser tab and one desktop-style client. It runs one recorded-run step, then lets both go. The test checks the server exits cleanly and leaves nothing behind.
- **Recovery test.** It kills the server mid-run and starts it again. A leftover registration may only be taken over once its owner is confirmed gone, and the run must reopen with only its finished steps.
- **Documentation.** It brings the READMEs and the self-review plan up to date, ticks off the app-server units with the commits they landed in, and adds a "Status, 16 Nov" section to the plan listing what's merged and what remains.

Nothing is blocked on you. Two things to know:
- All of this sits on the `civic/controller-2026-11-15` branch. Nothing has been pushed or merged into your main checkout, so your live instance on 3012 is unchanged.
- Your private Orca adapter will start using the cleanup helper for old preview builds once this work reaches your main checkout.

content.text:
The last app-server step (S10 U6) is committed (`df5a9060`), and its sign-off is waiting for a quiet machine. It isn't merged, and its new checks haven't run yet.

**What U6 checks:** an empty app installs CIVIC from git and goes through the whole life of the shared server.
- One browser tab and one desktop-style client attach, and a recorded-run step runs.
- The server is killed mid-run and started again:
  - the leftover registration is taken over only once its owner process is gone;
  - the run reopens with only its finished steps;
  - a run whose saved history doesn't match is refused.
- When the last client leaves, the server exits and leaves no registration, lock or worker processes behind.

**What else it changed:**
- **Docs:** the READMEs and the self-dogfood plan now describe what exists. The plans now record what landed where and what's still open.
- **Lint:** the new check had eight lint findings, which I fixed in the code; the baseline is unchanged.

The sign-off includes the install check, so it also runs U6's new checks. If it passes, U6 merges, and every slice in the rebuild plan will be on the controller branch.

### Status, 16 Nov

Merged: tooling and dependency updates (S1/S1b), baseline checks (S2), the single
workspace (S3), core and request machine (S4), Effect MCP (S5), self-review picker
(S6), source-to-element (S7), backend coverage (S8), preview lifecycle and bounded
retention (S9/S9b), harness integrations (S11, `8375aea2`), and coordinator tools
(S11b, `267d4563`, base fix `94875c8d`). S10 U1/U2 landed in `8bade120`; run
supervision in `e61e6847` with corrections `24d35503` and `62739c80`; managed
hosting in `dc55e5b3`; browser/Electron attachment in `613fb176`. Checkbox replay
was corrected in `8aed9b23`; layering cleanup landed in `050fc5d5`.

Remaining: U6's installed-consumer candidate and final acceptance/signoff,
including macOS sleep/wake, further S12 baseline cleanup, adoption of the shared
signoff package when available, and the owner decision about private-store
retention adoption/deletion. This list records merges, not fresh suite results.

Grounded at `f749b770` (this branch). Counts are from `grep` over tracked source, not lint output.

| Area | Today | Target | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Graph, importers, records (`graph/`, `importers/`, `review/src/store.ts`…) | Plain TypeScript, pure functions, `node --test` | Same | **Keep.** No Effect or XState here; a lint rule keeps it that way. `graph/src/validate.ts` (1057 lines) is a later candidate for Effect `Schema` only if it deletes code. |

U6's sign-off hasn't started at all. It has spent the whole 40 minutes waiting for its turn.

- **What it's waiting behind:** Orca is landing one branch after another. Its current sign-off, for its `homefold` branch, has been running for about 16 minutes. Before that it signed off its Effect 4.1 branch.
- **Load:** about 11, mostly Orca's browser tests.
- **How the wait works:** it only starts when load is below 6 and no CIVIC or Orca sign-off is running. Your rule says not to run heavy suites alongside Orca's sign-offs. While Orca keeps landing back to back with load above 6, CIVIC's turn never comes.
- **When it does run:** CIVIC's own sign-off takes about 4–5 minutes. The rest of tonight's delay has been this waiting.

**Decision for you:** three ways to get U6 through.

1. **Keep waiting.** It runs in the first quiet gap. That's safe, but there's no telling when, while Orca is landing.
2. **Run in the gap between Orca sign-offs.** Start as soon as no Orca sign-off is running, at any load, with a load cap of about 10 instead of 6, and still only one CIVIC heavy run at a time. CIVIC never overlaps an Orca sign-off; it just doesn't wait for the machine to fully settle. This is what I'd pick.
3. **Run alongside Orca now,** with fewer test workers. It's fastest, but it breaks your rule. Both sign-offs would also be slower and flakier; the browser tests failed several times tonight just from load.

I'm checking whether `install-managed.mjs` has a real bug: it resolves `effect` via `createRequire` from the installed package path. Under pnpm, that path is a symlink into the `.pnpm` store, so resolution may search the wrong `node_modules` unless the real path is used.

I'm going to check how `installed` is defined, since the fix is to realpath it before calling `createRequire` so resolution starts from the real store path instead of the pnpm symlink.

The trial passed on load, with no test failures, so the real bug is in U6's new check, which starts Node's lookup from the symlinked install path instead of the real one. I'm switching that lookup to the real path now.

input.task:
Bounded implementation worker for CIVIC (this checkout). Close three known gaps recorded in docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md and docs/integrations/orca-proposal.md "Known limit" (read AGENTS.md, docs/decisions/0022, the 18 Oct app-server plan's AE list). Everything they build on is merged: managed host (packages/canvas/server managed-host/registration/presence files, control socket), browser tab presence, Electron main attached (packages/local, `CIVIC_TEST=1 pnpm --dir packages/local run test:electron`), coordinator MCP resources (review/src/coordinator*.ts, review/src/mcp.ts).

1. **Coverage notifications for preview-only replays:** a replay saved only inside a running preview's store must also trigger `notifications/resources/updated` for `civic://coverage/{project}` (and anything else that reads that store). Watch that store's replay folder the same scoped, debounced way the existing watchers do (Effect scope, fs.watch, Schedule debounce, closed on unsubscribe and stdin end; no polling, no raw timers). Add it to the coordinator test, and delete the "Known limit" paragraph from docs/integrations/orca-proposal.md once it works.
2. **Vite restart with a connected desktop client** (KTD8): a test where a desktop-style client (bearer capability over the control socket) and a browser tab stay attached while the managed host restarts its Vite viewer generation (trigger it the way a source/config change does); the host process, its registration and the clients' connections survive; the tab sees the new generation; runs are not rebound to new code.
3. **Hidden tabs stay attached, frames never attach:** a browser test: a hidden top-level tab keeps its presence connection; a preview iframe inside the canvas and a capture browser do not create presence connections (count connections at the host).

Real processes, sockets and browsers; no mocks; temp stores; kill only what your tests start; Electron tests must run with CIVIC_TEST=1 (no native dialogs on the owner's screen). New code lint-clean: `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs` must pass. Anything the installed server loads stays plain JavaScript.

Rules: never change HOME; temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC, the running 3012 instance, or any .civic-canvas folder; installs only inside this worktree (`pnpm --dir packages install`); ≤2 test workers, one Electron at a time (the owner allowed running alongside other sign-offs tonight, so the load gate is not required). Another worker is changing lint-baseline tooling, the plan doc and raw timers in server code — avoid bin/lint-baseline.mjs and the plan doc. Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments. Don't run the full suites.

Bounded implementation worker for CIVIC (this checkout). Three independent follow-ups to docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md (read §3, the "Status, 16 Nov" note, AGENTS.md, docs/decisions/0022). Do all three; a blocker in one does not stop the others.

1. **Effect diagnostics under TypeScript 7.** `@effect/language-service` supports only TS 5/6; its README directs TS 7 users to `@effect/tsgo` (Effect Language Service for TypeScript-Go, latest 0.69.0, bin `effect-tsgo`). Add `@effect/tsgo` as a dev dependency where Effect is used (packages/core, packages/canvas, review — or once at the workspace root package `packages/package.json` if it can check several projects), read its installed README for the CLI diagnostics mode, and wire it into those packages' `check` so `pnpm --dir packages run check` runs it. If pnpm refuses it for release age, add it to `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` in packages/pnpm-workspace.yaml with a one-line reason. Existing diagnostics: fix if few and mechanical; otherwise extend bin/lint-baseline.mjs to count them per rule/file in the same shrink-only baseline (with a fixture test in scripts/lint-baseline.test.mjs). If it truly cannot run here, report the exact error and continue with items 2 and 3.
2. **Plan tidy:** move the "Status, 16 Nov" section from the middle of §1 (before the audit table) to the end of the document; update it: U6 landed in `117351ef` (install-and-recovery checks from a git-installed canvas); sign-offs ran alongside Orca's at the owner's request on 16 Nov; remaining work: hooks enablement and private-adapter adoption after the branch reaches main, Orca-side wiring (docs/integrations/orca-proposal.md), the shared sign-off package (§6b), proving the real-agent loop, Vite restart with a connected desktop client, hidden-tab/frame exclusion test, coverage notifications for preview-only replays (another worker is closing the last three), sleep/wake, and the Effect diagnostics outcome from item 1.
3. **Raw timers:** shrink `architecture/raw-timer` entries in lint-baseline.json (13 today) to zero in server/CLI code by replacing raw setTimeout/setInterval with Effect Schedule/Clock or a scoped Effect sleep, keeping behaviour; leave browser UI files alone; then `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs --update` (refuses increases). Run the tests of each file you change.

Rules: never change HOME; temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC or any .civic-canvas folder; installs only inside this worktree (`pnpm --dir packages install`); ≤2 test workers (the owner allowed running alongside other sign-offs tonight; no load gate required). Another worker is adding tests under packages/local, packages/canvas/server managed-host files and review/src/coordinator* — avoid those files. Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments. Don't run the full suites.

Report only: each item's outcome, diagnostics counts, raw-timer count before→after, commands with pass/fail, blockers.

content.text:
Backend coverage is built and merged on the controller branch. It isn't in `main` yet, so your live instance on 3012 doesn't have it. Notifications for runs replayed only inside a preview are the one open gap, and a worker is closing it now.

**What it answers:** for each journey, which server routes, handlers and RPCs its recorded runs actually reached, and which operations no journey reaches. A screen with good coverage can no longer hide a server path nobody tested.

**How it's worked out (no hand-written lists):**
- **The list of operations** comes from the project's own code:
  - Server functions are found automatically from the code (`createServerFn`).
  - HTTP routes and RPCs come from the route tables the project names in its CIVIC config. The Tasks and Team board examples now handle requests from their own tables, 3 and 5 routes, and CIVIC reads the same tables.
- **What counts as reached** comes from recorded runs:
  - Only runs that replayed successfully count. A replay that went off course counts up to the step where it diverged.
  - A request that got a 400-or-above response doesn't count.
  - Routes with parameters, such as `/tasks/:id`, are matched properly.

**Where you see it:**
- `civic coverage --backend` on the command line.
- A server section in the canvas coverage panel, in plain words, with file paths under Details.
- For agents: the `backend_coverage` MCP tool. Coordinators such as Orca also get a combined `coverage` tool (screens, journeys and backend), and can subscribe to it for change notices.

**Proven by tests:**
- On the Reading list example, one server function is deliberately never called. A real browser records and replays a journey, and the report names exactly that function.
- A replay that diverges counts only up to where it diverged.
- The Tasks, Team board and Reading list record-and-replay flows all pass.
- The CLI and the MCP tool give the same answer.

**Gaps and limits:**
- **Notifications for preview-only replays:** a run replayed only inside a preview shows up when coverage is read, but doesn't yet send a change notice. Follow-up B is fixing this now.
- **Only as good as the recordings:** with no recorded runs, every operation shows as unreached.
- **Opt-in for routes:** projects must name their route tables in their CIVIC config. Server functions need nothing.
- **Not tried on Orca or Laundry yet:** those projects are private, so checking them is a local run in your stores. Neither currently names its route tables.
- **No RPC example:** the config format supports RPCs, but no example project produces any yet. Only server functions and HTTP routes are exercised.

input.title: Fix presence lost on Vite restart (KTD8)
input.task:
Bounded fix worker for CIVIC (this checkout). HEAD is a WIP commit "wip: Close coverage-notice and hidden-tab gaps; Vite-restart presence test fails". One test fails: packages/canvas/server/managed-clients.check.mjs, subtest "adapter config restart retains host, registration, control connections and original run binding" (around line 117): after the managed host restarts its Vite viewer generation (adapter entry change → `select` with `restarting: true`), the host process, registration, desktop socket (readyState OPEN), the tab's control socket (not closed, one socket) and the run journal all survive — but the host's client count drops from 2 to 1.

Controller's diagnosis (verify, don't assume): both sockets are still open on the client side, so the host is losing track of a live client, not the client disconnecting. KTD8 in docs/plans/2026-10-18-0515-feat-effect-app-server-lifecycle-plan.md requires the stable Node listener, the control socket and server identity/presence to live in the host's scope, with Vite in middleware mode replaced per generation. Likely cause: some presence/client registry, ticket issuance, or the count endpoint is created per viewer generation (inside the Vite/middleware setup, e.g. via the review server or connector created per generation) instead of once per host, so a new generation starts with an empty registry or counts only its own; or the old generation's disposal releases clients it doesn't own. Read the managed-host, presence and registration modules under packages/canvas/server/, canvas-host.mjs, and the shell review middleware ticket issuance, find where client presence is owned, and fix it at the root so presence belongs to the host's Effect scope for its whole lifetime and survives generation replacement. **Fixed (tests pass):**

Hot reload works in managed mode: add a check that editing a canvas source file during a managed session hot-updates the open tab without a full reload and without dropping its control connection (count stays 2).
