content.text:
I didn't accept the fix, so the connection bug from Vite restarts is still open. A new worker is doing it the way the design intends.

**The cause:** each time the server restarts Vite, Vite's hot-reload channel goes away with the old copy and tells open tabs to reload. The reload hit the server's "Starting" page while the new Vite wasn't ready yet. That threw the page away, and with it the tab's connection. The worker found this; it wasn't that the server forgot the client.

**Why I rejected the fix:** it switched hot reload off entirely in desktop and managed mode. Your edits would have needed a manual reload there. The app-server design (KTD8) says the opposite: hot reload should hang off the long-lived server so it survives Vite restarts.

[KTD8: keep hot reload across Vite restarts](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3Ab11f2416-b73d-4e4c-a395-658be25f9d5c) is to:
- attach hot reload to the long-lived server;
- hold page requests briefly during a restart instead of answering "Starting", with a clear error only if the new Vite misses its deadline;
- check that a restart never drops clients that are still connected;
- add a test that editing a file in managed mode hot-updates the open tab without a full reload or a dropped connection.

**Waiting to batch with it:**
- Follow-up A2: Effect's diagnostics, timer cleanup and the plan tidy-up. Committed, but not signed off.
- The two gaps already closed in Follow-up B: coverage notices for preview-only replays, and the hidden-tab and frame test.

**Two flaky results** turned up in that worker's run, and both passed when run again on their own:
- a desktop test reopening a window;
- one sign-in test in the canvas suite.

The batch sign-off will show whether they recur.

input.task:
Bounded fix worker for CIVIC (this checkout). First confirm HEAD is e8cf1496 "wip: Close coverage-notice and hidden-tab gaps; Vite-restart presence test fails" and that packages/canvas/server/managed-clients.check.mjs exists; if not, stop and report. Then `pnpm --dir packages install`.

The failing test: managed-clients.check.mjs subtest "adapter config restart retains host, registration, control connections and original run binding": after the managed host restarts its Vite viewer generation, the host's client count drops from 2 to 1. Known facts: HMR is already attached to the host's stable listener (`hmr: { server: listener }` in packages/canvas/server/app-server-main.mjs); `presence.revoke()` only clears pending tickets and fences new attachments, it does not release existing clients. Cause found earlier: when the old generation closes, the open tab reloads; that reload reaches the host's `handle` while `current` is null and gets `503 Starting`, the page unloads and its control connection closes, so presence correctly releases it. A rejected earlier fix disabled HMR for the managed viewer — do NOT do that (KTD8 in docs/plans/2026-10-18-0515-feat-effect-app-server-lifecycle-plan.md keeps HMR on the stable listener).

Fix it at the root:
1. During a restart, hold incoming viewer requests (HTTP) until the new generation is ready instead of answering 503 — bounded by the KTD5 boot deadline (60 s) using Effect (no raw timers); after the deadline answer with a clear plain-words error. Requests during normal serving are unaffected.
2. Avoid a needless full reload when only the generation changes, if Vite lets you (e.g. the old generation's close shouldn't broadcast `full-reload`); if a reload is unavoidable, it must land on the new generation's page (guaranteed by 1).
3. The tab's document may reload but its control connection must re-attach within the presence grace window, or not drop at all; the restart subtest asserts the count is 2 afterwards. Add a check that editing a canvas source file during a managed session hot-updates the open tab (HMR) without dropping its control connection.
Keep: generation fencing (old runs refuse changed source), single-use tickets, no secrets in URLs/logs, plain JavaScript for anything the installed server loads.

Verify (under `node bin/with-temp-root.mjs`, concurrency 1): managed-clients.check.mjs (all subtests), app-server.check.mjs, service-registration.check.mjs, runtime-lifecycle.check.mjs, `(cd packages/canvas && vp test run --maxWorkers=1 server/client-presence.test.ts server/lifecycle.test.ts server/lifecycle-scope.test.ts)`, review/test/coordinator.test.ts, `CIVIC_TEST=1 … packages/local/desktop-lifecycle.electron.mjs` (one Electron at a time), `pnpm --dir packages run check`, `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs`.

content.text:
The last worker made no changes, because I started it from the wrong place. My own checkout was back on the controller branch when I launched it, so it got the wrong code and correctly stopped.

It still found something useful while it checked:
- Hot reload already runs through the long-lived server.
- The step that runs on restart only cancels passes that haven't been used yet. It doesn't disconnect anyone already attached.

So the remaining problem is narrow. While a new copy of Vite starts, the server answers page requests with "Starting". A tab that reloads at that moment lands on that page and loses its connection.

I've now started [KTD8: hold requests during Vite restart](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3Ab11f2416-b73d-4e4c-a395-658be25f9d5c) from the right branch, after first switching my checkout to it. It's told to confirm the starting commit before doing anything. It will:
- hold page requests during a restart until the new Vite is ready, up to 60 seconds, then show a clear error;
- avoid a needless full reload when only Vite restarted;
- add a check that editing a file in managed mode hot-updates the open tab without dropping its connection.

Hot reload stays on.

When it's back, three things get one combined sign-off:
- this fix;
- the two gaps already closed in Follow-up B;
- Follow-up A2 (Effect's own checks, removing most raw timers, tidying the plan).

- `d4bd9b37` (Follow-up A2): Effect's own diagnostics in the checks, server raw timers cut from 13 to 4, and the plan's status note updated.
- `bfdc024d`: the restart fix, plus the two gaps closed earlier:
  - coverage notices for runs replayed only in a preview;
  - the test that hidden tabs stay attached while preview frames and capture browsers never attach.

If it passes, the controller branch moves to that tree.

content.text:
The rebuild is done. Every slice of the plan is merged on the CIVIC controller branch `civic/controller-2026-11-15`. Nothing is in `main` or pushed, so your live CIVIC on 3012 still runs the old code. One batch of follow-ups is waiting to be signed off.

**Built and merged:**
- **Foundations:**
  - Vite+ tooling, all dependencies updated, and one install for all of CIVIC.
  - Lint checks against a baseline that can only shrink, now including Effect's own checks.
  - A shared state-machine core, and the MCP server rebuilt on Effect.
- **Source-to-element:** pick an element and get the file and line that drew it, or go from a file or a diff to the screens it affects. CIVIC can now review its own screens as a project.
- **Backend coverage:** which server routes and functions each journey reaches, and which none do. It's worked out from your code and from recorded runs, and you can see it on the command line, in the coverage panel, and from agents.
- **Agent tools and Orca:**
  - One MCP server for every agent tool, tested against a misbehaving agent.
  - The CIVIC side of the Orca hand-off: review sessions, work-item links, changed screens and notifications. The Orca-side wiring is written up as a proposal.
- **Shared app server and desktop app:**
  - One server per store, shared by browser tabs and the desktop app.
  - Recorded runs are managed safely across restarts and recovered after a crash.
  - The desktop window shows the branch name and uses its own profile per worktree.
  - All of this is proven from a copy of CIVIC installed from git.
- **Fixes found along the way:**
  - Checkbox replay was broken.
  - An agent could slip an option into git through `changed_screens`.
  - The desktop app could crash on a window event arriving after the window closed.
  - A git-installed canvas couldn't start its server.
  - Stale Orca preview folders: 75 moved to your Trash, about 1.3 GB.

**While you're away:**

content.content:
**What it is:** anti-slop is an Oxlint plugin (JavaScript plugins loaded through Oxlint's `jsPlugins`, not ESLint) with opinionated rules that reject low-evidence TypeScript and JavaScript patterns that coding agents often write. It is a fork of [dmmulroy/anti-slop](https://github.com/dmmulroy/anti-slop), maintained by Kyle Mistele. The fork adds LLM-judged rules, more Effect rules, Martin Fowler code-smell rules, and diff rules.

**License:** MIT.

**Installation:** The project says it is "meant to be vendored, not installed from npm." Options:
- An agent skill: `npx skills add K-Mistele/anti-slop --skill install-anti-slop`
- A copy script, `scripts/install.mjs`, which copies the plugin into your repo (for example, `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/`)
- A manual clone and copy, plus `oxlint` and `@oxlint/plugins` at the same exact version

It requires Node 22.18 or later. The examples use Oxlint 1.93.0, while upstream is tested with 1.86.0. A TypeScript `oxlint.config.ts` also needs `"type": "module"` in `package.json`.

**Rules (verbatim names):**

*Core (`anti-slop`)*: `max-ternary-depth`, `no-array-filter-map`, `no-chained-type-assertions`, `no-conditional-spread`, `no-disabled-type-assertion-rules`, `no-known-value-widening`, `no-module-mocking`, `no-object-parameters`, `no-reduce-accumulator-copy`, `no-reflect-apply`, `no-reflect-get`, `no-reprovide-ambient-service`, `no-runtime-typeof`, `no-shape-in-symbol-names`, `no-unknown-parameters`, `no-unknown-returns`, `no-unknown-type-aliases`, `no-unsafe-dictionary-type`, `no-widen-then-assert`, `require-readable-spacing`, `require-safety-comment-for-type-assertion`

*Effect (`anti-slop-effect`)*: `no-manual-effect-error-tag`, `no-manual-tag-comparison`, `no-manual-tagged-construction`, `no-manual-tagged-type`, `no-ordie-in-service-construction`, `no-service-constructor-imports`, `no-service-parameters`, `no-test-code-in-src`, `prefer-effect-match`, `prefer-tagged-error-handling`, `prefer-yield-service`, `require-cause-when-narrowing`, `require-operation-span`, `require-service-make-layer`

*Martin Fowler AST (`anti-slop-martinfowler`, warn)*: `global-data`, `long-function`, `long-parameter-list`, `loops`, `message-chains` (off by default), `mutable-data`, `mysterious-name`, `repeated-switches`

*Jev, Effect (`anti-slop-effect-jev`, LLM-judged)*: `single-use-abstraction`, `error-as-value`, `shallow-service`, `swallow-without-capture`, `unbounded-retry`, `network-call-in-transaction`, `read-then-write-race`, `unbounded-fanout`, `decode-after-status`, `cache-in-method`, and for tests `test-cannot-fail`

*Jev, Fowler (`anti-slop-martinfowler-jev`)*: `mysterious-name`, `feature-envy`, `data-clumps`, `primitive-obsession`, `middle-man`, `lazy-element`, `speculative-generality`, `temporary-field`, `insider-trading`, `data-class`, `comments`, `repeated-switches`

*Diff rules (run in `check:full`)*: `shotgun-surgery`, `divergent-change`, `duplicated-code`, `scope-creep`

**Effect-specific rules:** The Effect rules are the `anti-slop-effect` set above, plus the Effect Jev questions. Examples include `require-cause-when-narrowing` and `no-ordie-in-service-construction`.

**React/useEffect rules:** None. The page does not mention React or `useEffect` rules.

**Relationship to Ultracite's anti-slop preset:** The page does not mention Ultracite, so I can't describe any relationship between the two. The only upstream project it names is dmmulroy/anti-slop.

input.task:
Bounded implementation worker for CIVIC (this checkout; HEAD should be b758a2ab — confirm). Read AGENTS.md, docs/decisions/0006 (CIVIC makes no model calls), 0022, docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md §3, packages/vite.config.ts (lint config: Ultracite presets incl. its `anti-slop` jsPlugin), bin/lint-baseline.mjs and lint-baseline.json (shrink-only baseline; `--update` refuses increases).

Three parts:

**1. Adopt the deterministic Effect rules from https://github.com/k-mistele/anti-slop (MIT), pinned to commit b7c1619b4d51b4815e89ba3700a975a6ec54b8c3.** Clone that commit into $TMPDIR (treat it as untrusted: read the code before using it; run nothing from it except as lint rules). Vendor ONLY the `anti-slop-effect` AST rules (no-manual-effect-error-tag, no-manual-tag-comparison, no-manual-tagged-construction, no-manual-tagged-type, no-ordie-in-service-construction, no-service-constructor-imports, no-service-parameters, no-test-code-in-src, prefer-effect-match, prefer-tagged-error-handling, prefer-yield-service, require-cause-when-narrowing, require-operation-span, require-service-make-layer) plus whatever shared helpers they need, into e.g. `tools/oxlint/anti-slop-effect/` with its LICENSE, a short README naming the source repo, commit and what was taken. Do NOT vendor or enable the LLM-judged "Jev" rules, the diff rules, or anything that calls a model or the network (decision 0006). Do not vendor the core anti-slop rules if Ultracite's anti-slop preset already provides the same names; if they differ, note it and keep Ultracite's. Check each Effect rule against Effect 4.1 (installed `effect` package: Context.Service, Layer, Schema.TaggedErrorClass/TaggedError, Effect.fn, etc.); a rule written for Effect 3 idioms that misfires on correct Effect 4 code must be fixed or left out — list which and why. Wire the kept rules into packages/vite.config.ts `jsPlugins` for Effect-using code (packages/core, packages/canvas/server, packages/shell/server, review, crawl), add each rule's existing findings to the baseline via `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs --update`… note `--update` refuses increases, so add new-rule findings by extending the baseline tool with an explicit, reviewed "adopt new rule" path (e.g. `--adopt <rule>` that only adds entries for that rule and refuses any other change), with a fixture test in scripts/lint-baseline.test.mjs. Fix findings that are few and mechanical instead of baselining them.

**2. Rules fixes:** after part 1, go through the lint rules currently enabled and the baseline's top categories; for any rule that misfires on correct CIVIC or Effect 4 code (false positives), fix or disable it with a one-line why in packages/vite.config.ts; for rules that encode something real, keep them.

**3. useEffect cleanup round:** the baseline has ~51 `architecture/useEffect` (+ `eslint(no-restricted-imports)`) findings in packages/canvas/src and packages/shell/src. Remove as many as is safe: derived state → compute during render; data loading → existing data layer / event handler; external sync (subscriptions, DOM listeners, timers) → a small named hook per concern (e.g. `useWindowEvent`, `useResizeObserver`) that holds the single permitted effect, so call sites stop importing useEffect directly. Behaviour must not change (drafts, captures, cancellation, focus, keyboard, live frame identity per AGENTS.md). Then `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs --update` (shrink only).

Verify: `pnpm --dir packages run check`; `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs`; `pnpm --dir packages --filter @civic/canvas test` and `--filter @civic/shell test` (these include real-browser checks — run them with ≤2 workers; wait for `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/REDACTED/8f3b2eca-0508-4f5d-8344-d9ed70c2da42/scratchpad/gate.sh` first, it may wait long, that's fine); scripts/lint-baseline.test.mjs.

Rules: never change HOME; temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC, the running 3012 instance, or any .civic-canvas folder; installs only inside this worktree; no new runtime dependencies (dev-only for lint if the vendored rules need `@oxlint/plugins` — check whether Ultracite already provides it). Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments.

Report only: rules vendored (and left out, why), baseline counts before→after per category, useEffect count before→after and the named hooks added, commands with pass/fail, blockers.

content.text:
Yes, it's worth adopting, but only its 14 rule-based Effect checks. A worker is doing that now, together with the rule fixes and the `useEffect` cleanup.

**What the repo is:** an MIT-licensed Oxlint plugin that you copy into your repo rather than install. It's a fork of `dmmulroy/anti-slop`. Our current Ultracite `anti-slop` rules look like they come from that original, since the rule names match the ones already in our lint results.

**What we're taking**
- **The 14 Effect checks.** For example:
  - `require-cause-when-narrowing` keeps the original error when an error is turned into another;
  - `prefer-tagged-error-handling` handles errors by their tag;
  - `no-ordie-in-service-construction` stops a service crashing the program while it's being set up;
  - `prefer-yield-service` and `require-service-make-layer` keep services built the standard way.

  They catch the same kinds of Effect mistakes Orca's audit turned up: failures that silently disappear, and errors that lose their original cause.
- **Pinned to one commit,** `b7c1619b`, copied into `tools/oxlint/anti-slop-effect/` with its license and a note saying where it came from.

**What we're not taking**
- **The rules a language model judges, and the rules that compare diffs.** They would make CIVIC's own checks call a model, which decision 0006 rules out. A model also won't give the same answer every time, and a baseline that can only shrink needs the same result on every run.
- **The Fowler code-smell rules.** They're warnings only, so I left them out to keep this round focused.
- **Anything for `useEffect`.** The repo has no `useEffect` rules, so CIVIC's own check stays.

[Adopt anti-slop Effect rules, fix rules, useEffect cleanup](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A38116112-c20b-4d7d-ac76-fdedaabfd6be) has three parts:
1. **Copy in the 14 Effect rules.**
   - It checks each one against Effect 4.1. A rule written for Effect 3 that wrongly flags correct Effect 4 code gets fixed or left out, with the reason recorded.
   - Each new rule's existing findings go into the baseline through a new, deliberate "adopt rule" step, so the "can only shrink" protection stays.
   - Findings that are few and easy get fixed instead.
2. **Fix the rules.** Any enabled rule that flags correct CIVIC or Effect 4 code gets fixed, or switched off with a one-line reason.
3. **The `useEffect` cleanup.** It removes as many of the 51 `useEffect` calls in the UI as is safe:
   - values worked out from other state get computed directly instead;
   - subscriptions, listeners and timers move into small named hooks, one per concern.

   Drafts, captures, focus and keyboard behaviour mustn't change.

It starts from the follow-up batch that's still waiting to be signed off. That batch lands first, once the machine is quiet. Then this work gets its own sign-off. The real-agent loop proof follows after that.

input.task:
Bounded investigation-and-fix worker for CIVIC (this checkout; confirm HEAD is b758a2ab). Read AGENTS.md. Three browser checks fail intermittently in the full sign-off run (`pnpm --dir packages --filter @civic/canvas run test:host`, i.e. `node --test --test-concurrency=2 "server/*.check.mjs"` under bin/with-temp-root.mjs), even at moderate load (6–8), while they usually pass run alone:
- packages/canvas/server/managed-clients.check.mjs — "hidden top-level tabs retain their hold; nested canvas, preview and capture frames acquire none" (timeout waiting for `locator('iframe').nth(1).contentFrame().locator('[data-rehearsal-ready="true"]')`) and "canvas source hot-updates without dropping the control connection" (page.waitForFunction 30 s timeout). These tests are new (added in the two latest commits; see `git log -3`).
- packages/canvas/server/viewport-controls.check.mjs:169 — "custom dimensions reject invalid input and retain legacy preferences until a valid resize" (timeout waiting for button 'Viewport · Custom · 480 × 800'). This one is older; it may be affected by the new files running alongside it.

Goal: find the actual cause and fix it so these checks pass reliably in the real sign-off configuration (concurrency 2, alongside the other server/*.check.mjs files), without weakening what they assert.
1. Reproduce: run the full `test:host` command several times and each failing file alone and in pairs (e.g. managed-clients with viewport-controls), recording pass/fail. On a failure, capture evidence (Playwright trace or screenshot + page console + host log) into $TMPDIR.
2. Look for shared state between concurrently running checks: fixed ports, a shared store or registration path, shared browser profile, global `~/.civic`/TMPDIR paths, a process-wide singleton, HMR/file watchers on the same source files (the hot-update test edits a canvas source file — does that edit reach other concurrently running canvas hosts that watch the same packages/canvas/src, triggering reloads in their pages? If so, that test must edit a private copy, not shared repo source), or the managed host's restart affecting other hosts.
3. Fix at the root (isolate state, edit only a temp copy of source, wait on real readiness signals instead of fixed waits). Do not raise timeouts as the fix unless the evidence shows the work genuinely needs longer, and say so.
Verify: the full test:host command passes 3 times in a row; managed-clients.check.mjs and viewport-controls.check.mjs pass alone; `pnpm --dir packages run check` and `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs` pass.

Rules: never change HOME; temp only in $TMPDIR; ephemeral ports only, never 3012 3013 4317 5733 4417 5734 10448 10449; never touch /Users/taymoor/Projects/CIVIC, the running 3012 instance, or any .civic-canvas folder; installs only inside this worktree (`pnpm --dir packages install`); ≤2 test workers; before each full run, wait with `bash /private/tmp/claude-501/REDACTED/8f3b2eca-0508-4f5d-8344-d9ed70c2da42/scratchpad/gate10.sh` (no Orca sign-off running, load < 10). Kill only processes your runs start. Another worker is editing packages/vite.config.ts, lint tooling and canvas/shell UI files for a useEffect cleanup — avoid those files; if the fix needs them, report instead. Do NOT commit, push, merge or delegate; leave changes uncommitted. Short why-only comments.

Report only: reproduction table, root cause with file:line and evidence, the fix, commands with pass/fail.

The follow-up batch failed its sign-off a third time, so it still hasn't landed. This time the machine was fairly quiet, at load 6–8, so the cause isn't only load.

Three browser tests timed out:
- two of the new shared-server connection tests, the same ones as last time: "hidden tabs stay attached, frames never attach" and "editing a file hot-updates without dropping the connection";
- an older viewport test: "custom dimensions reject invalid input".

These tests usually pass when run on their own. The sign-off runs two test files at a time. My best guess is that the new hot-update test edits a real canvas source file, and other canvas servers running alongside are watching that same file. They would reload their own pages partway through their tests.

I've started [Make the managed-client and viewport checks reliable](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A0fc5146e-3a24-492d-b871-e21a3331032d%3Adelegate-task%3A1b782ab7-b882-4ce7-906d-9ff1155cc71f). It will:
- reproduce the failures the way the sign-off runs them, and capture evidence when a test fails;
- find whatever the test runs share: ports, stores, profiles, or files being watched;
- fix the cause itself. Longer timeouts only count as a fix if the evidence shows the work genuinely needs more time.
- run the full browser suite three times in a row as proof.

The batch lands once that fix is in.

Also still running: the worker adopting the Effect rules and cleaning up `useEffect`. It starts from the same batch, so both will go through sign-off together.

I think the root cause is occlusion: the test runs a real non-headless Chrome, so background throttling pauses requestAnimationFrame on the occluded window. The fix keeps the preview visible, disables occlusion with the backgrounding flag, and switches to timer polling, which seems reasonable. The viewport check still doesn't make sense to me, since it's an old test and might hit the same occlusion issue in another browser. I'll accept the fix, commit it on a fix branch from b758a2ab, and then merge.

content.text:
The worker found the real cause. The connection test uses a real Chrome window, and when the desktop hides that window, Chrome stops drawing it. Its embedded preview then never reported "ready", so the test timed out. In the hot-update test, the update actually happened, but the test's check for it relies on drawing, which had paused.

The fix lives entirely in that test file:
- it keeps the preview visible;
- it stops Chrome pausing a hidden window;
- it checks for the hot update on a timer instead of waiting for drawing.

The assertions and timeouts are unchanged. Those two connection tests then passed in every run: alone, and alongside the viewport test.

The viewport failure didn't happen again, so its cause is still unknown. It may be the same hidden-window pausing, since that test also runs a browser. Committing the fix and adding it to the batch, then running one sign-off.

content.text:
I found and fixed why two of the flaky shared-server browser tests failed. The batch still hasn't landed; its sign-off is waiting for no Orca sign-off and load below 10.

**What was wrong:** the connection test runs a real Chrome window. When that window was covered on the desktop, Chrome stopped drawing it.
- The embedded preview never reported "ready", so the first test timed out.
- In the hot-update test the update did arrive. The test's check for it waited on drawing, which had paused.

**The fix, in the test file only:**
- the preview stays in view;
- Chrome is told not to pause a covered window;
- the hot-update check polls on a timer instead of waiting for drawing.

The assertions and timeouts are unchanged. Afterwards the two connection tests passed alone (4 of 4), and with the viewport test alongside them (15 of 15).

**What's still open:**
- The worker couldn't run the full browser suite three times in a row, because Orca's sign-offs kept the machine busy. The sign-off will be the first full run with this fix.
- The viewport test that also failed didn't fail again, so its cause is still unknown. It may be the same covered-window pausing.

**Something you might notice:** this connection test opens a real Chrome window, because it needs Chrome's real tab visibility. You may see windows appear and disappear during sign-offs. They're the test's own temporary profile, not your Chrome.

The worker adopting the Effect rules and cleaning up `useEffect` is still running.

content.text:
The last piece of work, the Effect lint rules from anti-slop plus the `useEffect` cleanup, is committed and merged onto a candidate with the current controller branch, with no conflicts. Its sign-off and the desktop tests are waiting for no Orca sign-off and load below 10. Nothing from it has landed yet.

**What it adds:**
- **Effect rules:** 12 of anti-slop's 14 Effect rules now run on CIVIC's Effect code, copied in and pinned to one commit with its MIT license. They found 6 problems, and all 6 were fixed rather than added to the baseline.
- **Two rules left off:**
  - One treats every `makeX` function as a service, and CIVIC uses that name for plain factories too.
  - The other forbids tests that sit next to their source, which CIVIC does on purpose.
- **A rule switched off:** Ultracite's `no-runtime-typeof`. It flagged the plain `typeof` checks CIVIC uses to check inputs at its edges. That alone removes 159 findings. The baseline overall drops from 3,311 findings to 3,139.
- **Adding future rules safely:** the baseline now has a step that lets a new rule's existing findings be added, and nothing else.
- **`useEffect` cleanup:** the UI's `useEffect` calls drop from 51 to 45. They move behind three small named hooks: `useWindowEvent`, `useResizeObserver`, `useFrameKeydown`.

**Test results from the worker's run:**
- The shell tests (37) and review tests (10) pass.
- The canvas unit tests (95) pass.
- Of the canvas browser checks, 72 of 76 passed. The failures were the flaky connection tests, plus one camera test that passed when re-run. The worker started from a version without the fix for the connection tests, which has landed since; the candidate includes it.

**After this sign-off:** if it passes, I'll move the controller branch to it, write the handover in the plan, and stop. If it fails on something real, I'll fix it only if the fix is small. Otherwise I'll leave it on its branch and note it in the handover.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - The owner (15 Nov 2026) asked me to act as CIVIC's controller and rebuild CIVIC as an Effect.ts + XState + Electron project, like Orca.
   - CIVIC must be an MCP server with agent and harness integrations.
   - Decision 0006 still holds: CIVIC makes no model calls and launches no agents.
   - Build source-to-element: select an element and get its source file and line, and go from a file or diff to the elements it renders. These locations ride on comments and work requests. Try it on CIVIC's own UI first.
   - Build backend coverage: which routes, handlers and RPCs each journey exercises, and which none reach. Derive it from recorded runs plus the graph, never from hand-written lists.
   - Make CIVIC a project in its own picker.
   - Clean up the codebase using Orca's lessons:
     - corrections become checks with shrink-only baselines;
     - no useEffect, no raw timers, no vi.mock;
     - layering rules;
     - Effect language service;
     - e2e unmocked tests;
     - Vite+ everywhere;
     - typed commits;
     - land small, signed off;
     - resource frugality;
     - owner-facing text in everyday words.
   - Order: deliver a written plan first, then execute slice by slice, delegating to Codex workers (gpt-6.1-sol, worktree isolation).
   - Later additions:
     - Effect 4.1 and XState v6 beta; reuse Orca's w/effect-41 findings.
     - Update all dependencies.
     - Write a CIVIC ⇄ Orca integration contract, with the Orca-side wiring as a proposal only.
     - XState v6 agent guidance: machine checks assert transitionTargetsComplete and empty getMachineSerializationDiagnostics; failing sequences are saved and replayed.
     - Hooks: ship `.vite-hooks/<hook>.pre-entire` and an absolute core.hooksPath.
     - Keep bin/signoff; list requirements for the shared sign-off package instead.
     - Batch sign-offs by default and merge without rebase when there are no conflicts.
     - Approved deleting the stale orca-worktree folders ("Go").
     - Asked to list checkbox tapes ("sure").
     - Tried running sign-offs alongside Orca ("lets see how this goes").
     - Asked whether anything in k-mistele/anti-slop is worth adopting, to be combined with the rule fixes and the useEffect cleanup.
     - Most recently said Codex usage is below 50% weekly and that I'm close to wrapping up.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Effect 4.1 (^4.1.4): Scope, acquireRelease, Schedule, Clock, TestClock, and Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument for MCP.
   - XState 6.0.0-beta.3 and @xstate/effect 1.0.0-beta.2, pinned exact.
   - machineFromJSON with object transitions and plain guards.
   - @civic/core kernel (initial, decide, commit) and testing helpers (assertAnalysis, assertGraph, replayRegressions). Analysis assertions use transitionTargetsComplete and getMachineSerializationDiagnostics.
   - Vite+ 1.6.0: vp lint (oxlint with Ultracite presets), vp test, vp staged, vp hooks.
   - pnpm workspace in packages/ whose members include ../graph, ../review, ../importers and ../crawl. There is no root package.json, because the owner's main checkout has an untracked one.
   - Shrink-only lint baseline: bin/lint-baseline.mjs and lint-baseline.json. Architecture checks:
     - useEffect;
     - raw-timer;
     - module-mocking;
     - data-core;
     - browser-server;
     - outside-repo.
   - @effect/tsgo 0.69.0 for Effect diagnostics under TypeScript 7.
   - Git-installed canvas constraint: runtime code must be plain .mjs (Node won't strip types under node_modules). No @civic/core at runtime. Runtime deps use caret ranges or exact prerelease pins, never catalog: or workspace:.
   - Managed host: registration, lock, control socket, single-use tickets, desktop bearer capability, server and run machines.
   - Batch candidate branches get signed `--no-ff` merges, one bin/signoff, then a fast-forward of the controller.
   - Gate scripts in the scratchpad: gate.sh waits for load < 6 and no sign-off; gate10.sh waits for load < 10. Both match only real processes: `bash .../bin/signoff` or `node .../scripts/signoff.ts`.

   - Plans and decisions:
     - docs/plans/2026-11-15-effect-xstate-electron-rebuild.md: the plan (audit, slices S0–S12, §5b Orca contract, §6b shared sign-off requirements). Its final "Status, 16 Nov (handover)" section was written at the end, commit 045a9c5f.

     - bin/lint-baseline.mjs: architecture checker plus baseline compare. `--update` only shrinks; exemptions apply for test child_process and react-dom/server.
     - scripts/commit-type.ts and .vite-hooks/{commit-msg, commit-msg.pre-entire, pre-commit}.

     - review/src/preview/{lifecycle.ts, runtime.ts}.
     - review/src/mcp.ts: the Effect Schema TOOLS table; rows include elements, backend_coverage, the coordinator tools and resources.

   - **Load:** Orca's back-to-back sign-offs starved the strict gate. The trial of running alongside Orca worked at load 10–25 for some runs but flaked browser tests. Overnight I used gate10, which requires no Orca sign-off and load < 10.

Batch sign-offs by default: when several slices are ready, merge each branch as-is into one candidate branch (signed `--no-ff` merges, each slice keeps its own commits), run one `bin/signoff --no-post` on the candidate head, then fast-forward the controller branch to it. Do not rebase a branch onto the latest controller head unless the merge actually conflicts. If the batch fails, the failing test names the slice; fix or drop that slice and re-run.

**Why:** owner, 15 Nov 2026: "you should've been batching by default (and doing a git-merge like where a rebase is not needed if there's not conflicts)". Sign-offs wait for a quiet machine (load < 6, no other sign-off); queuing one per slice multiplied the waits and heavy CPU.

**How to apply:** "land each verified slice" means each slice lands as its own merge, verified by the candidate sign-off covering the exact landed tree; it does not mean one sign-off per slice. Related: [[tenet-load-gate]].

- **Why the tests looked slow:** each "15–17 minute" check matches a sleep stretch of 938–1023 seconds. The test timers kept counting while the machine slept, so they ran out. My two-hour limit also counted sleep time, which is why the run was stopped.
- **Re-run:** the old trial build was also missing the last two controller commits, including the fix for the flaky managed-client checks. I built a new signed one, `candidate/batch7` (`80fe2a42`), from the current controller plus the anti-slop branch. It's running through `bin/signoff` now, once load is below 10 and no other sign-off is running. `caffeinate` blocks idle and system sleep while it runs. It can't stop an overheating shutdown, so heat could still interrupt it.

I'll report back when the sign-off finishes. If it passes, I'll fast-forward the controller branch to it; nothing goes to `main` or gets pushed. If it fails, the failure will be real and I'll look into it then.

content.content:
## Status, 16 Nov (handover)

**Merged on `civic/controller-2026-11-15`** (each through `bin/signoff`; nothing pushed, nothing in `main`): every slice S0–S12 of this plan. Tooling and dependency updates (S1/S1b), shrink-only lint and architecture baselines (S2), one workspace (S3), the machine core and request machine (S4), the Effect MCP server (S5), CIVIC in its own picker (S6), source-to-element (S7), backend coverage (S8), the preview lifecycle and bounded build retention (S9/S9b), the shared app server and desktop app U1–U6 (S10), harness integrations (S11), the coordinator hand-off (S11b), and a first layering cleanup (S12). Follow-ups merged in `7c9a1442`: Effect diagnostics through `@effect/tsgo` 0.69.0 (10 recorded in the baseline), server raw timers 13 → 4, attached tabs and desktop surviving a Vite restart, coverage notices for preview-only replays, a hidden-tab and frame test, and a fix for the managed-client checks' covered-window rendering. Fixes found on the way: checkbox replay, a git option injection in `changed_screens`, a desktop crash on late window events, and git-installed canvases loading TypeScript.

**Not merged:** `chore/anti-slop-effect` (`174f6187`): 12 Effect rules vendored from k-mistele/anti-slop at `b7c1619b`, `no-runtime-typeof` off, a `--adopt` baseline path, and `useEffect` 51 → 45 behind `useWindowEvent`, `useResizeObserver` and `useFrameKeydown`. Its sign-off (`658e76f6`) stalled for 15–17 minutes per test in the canvas settings and viewport checks and in run-supervision's hung-operation check, which pass on `7c9a1442`. Likely cause: the `useEffect` changes in settings and viewport UI. Next step: run `viewport-controls.check.mjs` and `theme-settings.check.mjs` on that branch alone, find the hang, fix or split the lint rules from the hook changes.

**Owner decisions:** merge this branch into `main` and push; then enable hooks (`vp hooks enable`, absolute `core.hooksPath`) and adopt the retention helper in the private Orca adapter. Sign-off timing: wait for a quiet machine, or allow load below 10 when no Orca sign-off runs (used overnight 16 Nov). Two old dogfood recordings that tick a checkbox (`.civic-canvas/dogfood/run-E25HF5`) need re-recording or removal.

**Remaining work:** the Orca-side wiring ([proposal](../integrations/orca-proposal.md)); adopting the shared sign-off package (§6b); proving the real-agent loop end to end; sleep and wake; the viewport check that failed once without reproducing; the 60 second restart deadline path; source-to-element and backend coverage on Orca and Laundry (local, private); further baseline cleanup (useEffect, raw timers, about 3,300 lint findings).

content.text:
**In short:** the whole rebuild plan is merged on `civic/controller-2026-11-15`. Each piece went through `bin/signoff`. Nothing is in `main` or pushed yet.

**What landed**
- **Foundations:**
  - Effect 4.1 and XState v6 beta, and every dependency updated.
  - One workspace that runs on Vite+.
  - Typed commits and the sign-off script.
- **Code-health checks:**
  - Lint and architecture checks whose recorded counts can only go down, never up.
  - Effect's own code diagnostics.
  - Rules against `useEffect`, raw timers, module mocking, and wrong-way imports.
- **Core:** the shared state-machine core, the review request machine, and the MCP server built on Effect.
- **Features you asked for:**
  - CIVIC appears as a project in its own picker.
  - Source-to-element: pick an element to see its file and line, or go from a file or diff to what it renders. Comments and work requests carry those locations.
  - Backend coverage: which routes and handlers each journey reaches and which nothing reaches. It is worked out from recorded runs plus the code graph.
- **App and integrations:**
  - The preview lifecycle, with old builds cleaned up automatically.
  - The shared app server and desktop app, which now survive a Vite restart.
  - Agent and harness integrations, and handing a request to a coding agent.
- **Fixes found along the way:**
  - A git option injection in `changed_screens`.
  - The desktop crash from the error dialog you saw.
  - Checkbox replay.
  - Canvases installed from git failing to load.
  - Flaky browser checks.
- **Docs:** the CIVIC ⇄ Orca contract, written as a proposal only.

**In progress**
- **The anti-slop Effect rules plus the `useEffect` cleanup** (51 → 45). Its earlier "hang" was the machine sleeping, as you suspected. Its sign-off started at 11:52 with sleep blocked, and I'll merge it into the controller branch if it passes.

**Waiting on you**
1. Merge the controller branch into `main` and push. After that, the commit hooks can be switched on, and your private Orca adapter can use the cleanup helper.
2. Choose how sign-offs wait for the machine:
   - **Strict:** load below 6.
   - **Relaxed:** load below 10 with no Orca sign-off running, which is what I used overnight.
3. Re-record or delete the two old dogfood recordings that tick a checkbox.

**Work remaining** (none of it started)
- Wiring the Orca side of the integration, per the proposal.
- Moving to the shared sign-off package.
- Proving the real-agent loop end to end.
- Testing that the desktop app comes back cleanly after the machine sleeps and wakes.
- The 60-second restart deadline, which is untested.
- A viewport check that failed once and never again.
- Trying source-to-element and backend coverage on Orca and Laundry.
- Further cleanup: `useEffect`, raw timers, and about 3,300 lint findings.

The handover section of the plan still blames the anti-slop branch's code for the hang. I'll correct it once this sign-off result is in.

content.text:
The anti-slop batch failed its sign-off again, this time on two managed-viewer checks, so I haven't merged it. I've queued a re-run and will report back when it finishes.

- **What failed:** after a config restart, one check expected two connected viewer clients and found one. The next check then failed because of what the first left behind. Every other test passed.
- **Likely cause:** heavy load, not the branch's code.
  - An Orca sign-off started in the same second as ours, and load rose to 14. These checks have been flaky under that kind of load before.
  - The branch's `useEffect` changes only resize the desktop tab strip and fold the side outline on narrow windows. Neither touches how viewer clients connect.
- **Re-run:** it waits for load below 10 and no sign-off running, checks again 30 seconds later so the two can't start together, and keeps the machine awake.
- **If it passes:** I'll fast-forward the controller branch and correct the handover, which still blames this branch's code for the earlier hang.
- **If the same checks fail on a quiet machine:** I'll treat it as a real fault and investigate.

Next step: run `viewport-controls.check.mjs` and `theme-settings.check.mjs` on that branch alone, find the hang, fix or split the lint rules from the hook changes.

- **Second failure:** an Orca sign-off started in the same second as ours and pushed the load to 14, which broke the managed-viewer checks. Run alone, they pass.
- **One real bug:** the branch's new lint test only worked when run from the repo root. I fixed it in `cd7f27af`.

**How sign-offs run now:** they keep the machine from sleeping while they run. After the gate opens, they wait 30 seconds and check it again, so two sign-offs can't start in the same instant. Neither change is in the repo yet: both live in my temporary scripts, which go away with this session.

- **`candidate/batch7` branch:** it's fully merged, but the safety hook won't let me delete a branch without your approval. Run `git branch -d candidate/batch7` if you want it gone.

content.content:
# Delegation protocol

Delegate only when isolated context, specialization, useful parallelism, or disposable exploration outweighs coordination. Otherwise root works. Root remains controller, integrator, and completion owner. Each child satisfies one named evidence/signoff need rather than duplicating root work. A child has no controller, integration, landing, external-action, completion, or delegation authority.

Read-only is default. A mutation lease names its isolated worktree or paths, permitted edits and commands, required check, and stop condition. Independent isolated worktrees may hold concurrent bounded mutation leases only when their paths, decisions, dependencies, integration targets, landing surfaces, authority, and external effects do not overlap. A shared worktree has one writer. Root waits for every mutating lease to close before it integrates, lands, changes phase, operates on worktrees, or completes.

Before dispatch record goal, active stage, source or path, expected benefit, mode, ownership, allowed commands, forbidden paths or actions, named evidence/signoff need, required verification, and stop condition. An assessment is read-only evidence, not mutation authority. A child may not change instructions, provider state, configuration outside its lease, commit, push, merge, publish, use credentials, act externally, or delegate.

On crossed scope, competing ownership, or unauthorized action: interrupt, inspect status and diff, preserve unrelated work, and reject unverified output. Root verifies accepted evidence and the final diff.

Pass only needed context and use only completed results. A child stops when that need is met or its assignment ends. Return only conclusion or diff summary, evidence, verification, uncertainty, and blockers.

# Sign-off

Local checks for an exact Git commit, with reusable check results,
an optional area map, and a live status view. Requires Node 26.13.1 or later and Git.
Nothing is pushed. GitHub is contacted only with an explicit `--post` invocation.

## Project configuration

Commit `.signoff.json` on `main` before using the runner on a work branch:

```json
{
  "checks": [
    { "name": "check", "argv": ["pnpm", "check"] },
    { "name": "test", "argv": ["pnpm", "test"] },
    { "name": "build", "argv": ["pnpm", "build"] }
  ]
}
```

`checks` contains 1–32 checks with unique names. Each has an argv array (no shell
evaluation), optional repository-relative `cwd`, optional literal path prefixes
in `paths`, and an optional `timeoutMs` (positive integer, at most 24 hours).
Leading `NAME=value` argv words set environment variables. A check without
`paths` covers the whole tracked tree. `signoffOnly` is accepted for compatibility
with Orca's landing manifest; every configured check is eligible for sign-off.

The optional `areaMap` has the same shape as Orca's existing domain file:

```json
{
  "checks": [
    { "name": "check", "argv": ["pnpm", "check"] },
    { "name": "test", "argv": ["pnpm", "test"] }
  ],
  "areaMap": {
    "broad": ["src/"],
    "domains": [
      { "name": "docs", "match": "\\.md$", "checks": ["check"] },
      { "name": "source", "match": "^src/", "checks": "all" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The first matching domain for each changed file selects checks; an unknown file
keeps all eligible checks. Narrow check paths also select their checks. Existing
Orca maps can capture `(?<area>...)` to select `src/core/` test shards. Omitting the
map runs every check whose paths match. `--all` ignores only the area map.
Configuration is always read from `main`, including during `--verify`, so a work
branch cannot weaken its own checks. A config change on main invalidates records.

## Entry points

In another workspace, copy this package and use a root script like:

```ts
import { signoffMain } from "../packages/signoff/src/signoff.ts";
await signoffMain();
```

Run it from the repository root. Orca retains `node scripts/signoff.ts` and its
existing hooks through adapters that point to `.orca/landing.json` and
`.orca/signoff-domains.json`; those files do not need to be combined.

```sh
node scripts/signoff.ts --dry-run
node scripts/signoff.ts --fresh
node scripts/signoff.ts --all
node scripts/signoff.ts --verify <sha>
node scripts/signoff.ts --watch
node scripts/signoff.ts --post
```

`--dry-run` writes nothing. `--fresh` disables result reuse and the task cache.
`--post` is the owner's explicit authorization to call `gh api` and record a
successful `signoff` status for the checked commit. It requires an already
authenticated GitHub CLI, refuses test processes and dry runs, and never pushes,
fetches, changes protection rules, or comments on a PR. Posting failure leaves the
local result intact and exits unsuccessfully. Tests never invoke GitHub.

content.content:
local result intact and exits unsuccessfully. Tests never invoke GitHub.

A project that sets `"typedCommits": true` in its sign-off config has its commit titles after `main` checked before any check runs; other projects keep their own commit style. The exported `commitTypeMain`
supports a commit-msg hook. `statusMain` supports the separate status script and
the existing queued/held declarations. Results, fingerprints, logs, progress and
bounded cache files live in the Git common directory under `orca-signoff`, a
retained name so existing Orca records still work. This is local owner evidence,
not a signed attestation against a hostile owner process.

Fingerprints use Git content hashes and retain path-to-content validation. A move
outside a check's declared inputs can reuse its pass; moving an input reruns the
check, because paths affect imports and test discovery. Without a complete import
proof, shared scripts/configs remain inputs to every check. Dry-run reports
`reuse: same content as <sha>`.
Existing path-bound pass files and sign-off records remain readable.

When TypeScript 7 is already installed, one Git-backed module graph can prove
dependencies of literal Node commands, Node test lists, workspace Vite+ unit
commands, and Playwright commands. A complete proof binds discovery paths, every
resolved import and its content, package/TypeScript context, runner configuration,
setup/reporters, fixtures, lockfiles, tool versions and hashed environment values.
It replaces broad shared invalidation only for that command. Dynamic imports,
runtime I/O, plugins, aliases or exports with unproved runtime semantics, unknown
commands and missing tooling retain the original fingerprint and full command.
Browser proofs also include application/server code; unknown dependencies there
keep the entire browser check. No dependency is installed automatically.

For a complete test proof, passing files earn separate bounded cache entries.
Later runs execute only files without matching evidence and preserve the existing
shards, serial parts, browser lane and worker limits. Discovery changes invalidate
all file evidence, so new, renamed and removed tests cannot inherit another test's
pass. A failed or stopped check earns no new file passes. Old broad cache entries
cannot seed stronger graph evidence. `--fresh` bypasses both caches; `--all` keeps
its existing area-map meaning, and `--verify` retains its record contract.

Dry-run explains each graph reuse with `not affected: no import path from ...`
and prints each file decision and proof key. Closure evidence lives beside passes
in `proof-v1`, is pruned with them, and contains no environment values. Graph
failure is reported as `dependency proof unavailable`, with the original command
and reuse behavior preserved. The separate direct-import preflight only changes
execution order; it never supplies omission evidence.

A check that passes only on its one rerun is recorded as `flaky: true`, alongside
the existing `passed` state and `rerun` flag. Results and both status views show
the warning. Cached reuse retains it even after the original record is pruned.
This identifies flaky checks; arbitrary command output does not reliably identify
individual tests. The rerun policy and exact-commit verification are unchanged.

## Vite+ and related tests

Plain commands run sequentially; Playwright commands have their own browser lane.
To use Vite+ tasks, set `"vite": true` in the config and register the same checks
with `landingTasks(config.checks)` from the `./tasks` export in `vite.config.ts`.
The runner uses the project's `node_modules/.bin/vp` when present and otherwise
runs the commands directly. A mismatched candidate task definition is bypassed.
The cache is enabled only when Git sign-off storage lies outside the checkout;
every cache key includes the sign-off fingerprint and remote cache is disabled.

Set `"relatedTests": true` only for pnpm/Vitest workspaces using
`apps/*/src` and `packages/*/src`. Changed tests and tests directly importing changed
files run first, with at most 40 files and one worker per command. Orca's adapter
also supplies its server package and serial test file list to preserve its
existing crash/process test lanes. Neither convention is required for plain
command projects.

## Adoption notes

- CIVIC: express each graph/review/crawl/importer/demo/package gate as argv with
  its `cwd`, retaining its temporary-root wrapper and project-specific civic gate.
  Include browser evidence as a configured check when required; posting becomes
  explicit `--post`, while civic statuses and PR comments remain CIVIC's concern.
- laundry-app: use the three-check config above for `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`,
  then `pnpm build`, with no area map or Vite+ requirement. Its separate browser
  gate stays separate unless deliberately added to the checklist.

Goal: reduce the remaining `useEffect` calls in CIVIC's React UI (45 recorded in `lint-baseline.json` under the architecture rule for useEffect) without changing behaviour.

Repo: CIVIC, your isolated worktree (based on main 2302751b). Read AGENTS.md first. Scope (the only paths you may edit): `packages/canvas/src/**`, `packages/shell/src/**`, and `lint-baseline.json` (shrink only, via `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs --update`, which refuses growth).

How:
- Find every `useEffect` (`git grep -n useEffect -- packages/canvas/src packages/shell/src`).
- Remove the ones React does not need: state derived during render, work moved into the event handler that causes it, resets via `key`, subscriptions via `useSyncExternalStore`.
- Where an effect genuinely syncs with an outside system (window events, observers, keyboard), use the existing named hooks in `@civic/shell` (`use-window-event`, `use-resize-observer`, `use-frame-keydown`), the way `packages/canvas/src/app-canvas.tsx` and `desktop-project-tabs.tsx` already do.
- Do not invent a generic wrapper whose only purpose is hiding `useEffect` from the counter. A new named purpose hook is fine only if two or more call sites share it.
- Keep each change small and readable; match surrounding style; no new dependencies, raw timers or `vi.mock`.

Verify:
1. Install: `pnpm --dir packages install`.
2. Typecheck and lint: `pnpm --dir packages run check`.
3. Run the unit tests and browser checks under `packages/canvas` that cover every component you touched. The `*.check.mjs` files in `packages/canvas/server` are browser checks; find the right ones by grepping for the component or its UI text, and run them with `node --test <file>`.
4. Update the baseline with `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs --update`.

Machine sharing (required): before each browser check run, wait until the 1-minute load average (`sysctl -n vm.loadavg`) is below 10 and no process matching `bash .../bin/signoff` or `node .../scripts/signoff.ts` is running. Use at most 2 test workers. Never run `bin/signoff`.

Stop when every remaining `useEffect` is a genuine sync with something outside React.

Report:
- the before/after count;
- for each remaining `useEffect`, the file and a one-line reason it stays;
- the commands you ran and their results;
- anything uncertain.

input.task:
Goal: make CIVIC's managed host, desktop app and run supervision correct across the machine sleeping, test the 60-second restart deadline path, and remove the remaining raw timers in server code.

Repo: CIVIC, your isolated worktree (based on main 2302751b). Read AGENTS.md and docs/decisions/0022-effect-xstate-electron-foundations.md first.

Scope (the only paths you may edit):
- `packages/canvas/server/**`
- `packages/local/**`
- `lint-baseline.json` (shrink only, via `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs --update`)

Constraints:
- Runtime code in these folders must stay plain `.mjs`, because git-installed canvases cannot strip TypeScript under node_modules.
- No `@civic/core` at runtime. `effect` is an allowed runtime dependency.
- No `useEffect`, raw timers (`setTimeout`/`setInterval`) or `vi.mock` in new code.

Background, from 16 Nov: the machine slept for hours during a test run, and wall-clock timeouts fired as if the work had hung. Sleep looks like a sudden time jump: timers fire late and all at once.

Tasks:
1. Find every timeout, deadline, heartbeat, lease and poll in:
   - the managed host (`app-server-main.mjs`, server and run lifecycle, `runtime-service.mjs`);
   - the desktop main process (`packages/local/*.electron.mjs`, `desktop.mjs`);
   - run supervision.

   For each, decide what should happen after a long sleep. A client or run must not be declared dead, killed, or its lease revoked only because the clock jumped. On wake, re-check real liveness (the socket or process) before acting. In Electron, use `powerMonitor` 'suspend'/'resume' if the desktop needs it. Fix what is wrong.
2. The managed host holds requests during a restart up to a 60-second deadline. Add a test for the path where a restart exceeds that deadline: what do held requests and clients see? Use an injected or test clock (Effect `TestClock`, or the module's existing clock seam) so the test does not wait 60 seconds. If the behaviour is wrong, fix it.
3. Server raw timers: the lint baseline records 4 left. Replace them with Effect (`Effect.sleep`, `Schedule`, `Clock`) where that is clearer, the same way the earlier 13 → 4 reduction did. If one should stay, say why.

Verify:
1. Install: `pnpm --dir packages install`.
2. Typecheck and lint: `pnpm --dir packages run check`.
3. Run the server tests and `*.check.mjs` browser checks that cover the files you touched, with `node --test <file>`. This includes `managed-clients.check.mjs` and the run-supervision checks.
4. Run the `packages/local` tests.
5. Update the baseline with `node bin/lint-baseline.mjs --update`.

Machine sharing (required): before each browser or check run, wait until the 1-minute load average (`sysctl -n vm.loadavg`) is below 10 and no process matching `bash .../bin/signoff` or `node .../scripts/signoff.ts` is running. Use at most 2 test workers. Never run `bin/signoff`. Note that `managed-clients.check.mjs` is known to flake under heavy load (load above 12); if it fails, re-run once when the machine is quiet before you conclude.

Safety: never change HOME; temp files under $TMPDIR. Ephemeral ports only; never 3012, 3013, 4317, 5733, 4417, 5734, 10448 or 10449. Do not touch `~/Projects/CIVIC` (the owner's checkout), any `.civic-canvas/` folder, or Orca repos. Do not launch the real desktop app against the owner's data; tests use `CIVIC_TEST=1` and temp roots. Do not commit, push, merge, or change git config — leave changes uncommitted in the worktree.

Stop when the three tasks are done or you hit a decision that needs the owner.

Report:
- a table of each timer or deadline found, with its behaviour across sleep before and after;
- the diff summary;
- the commands you ran and their results;
- anything uncertain.

content.text:
Main is merged and pushed. `origin/main` is now at `2302751b`, a fast-forward of 71 signed commits. Nothing was listening on 3012, so your live instance wasn't running when the files changed. No GitHub checks run on `main`; the repo has only Dependabot.

**Your checkout needs an install before the next start:** the dependency updates mean `~/Projects/CIVIC` needs `pnpm --dir packages install` before you start CIVIC again.

**Cleanup:** I removed the scratch folder. The safety hook still refuses to delete the `candidate/batch7` branch, even with your go-ahead, and the approval code it asks for is yours to enter, not mine. Either run `git branch -d candidate/batch7` yourself, or run `dcg allow-once 082354` and I'll delete it. The branch is merged, so leaving it costs nothing.

**How strict is strict:** the 1-minute load average below 6, no other sign-off (CIVIC's or Orca's) running, at most 2 test workers, and one heavy suite at a time.
- In practice it almost never opens. With your usual apps running, this machine sits at a load of 6–8 even when nothing is being tested, and it's at 19 right now.
- I recommend the relaxed setting: load below 10, never alongside another sign-off, a second check 30 seconds later, and the machine kept awake.
  - Today's failure came from running alongside Orca's sign-off, not from the load level.
  - The worker adopting the shared sign-off package is building this in with 10 as the default, adjustable through `CIVIC_SIGNOFF_LOAD`. Tell me if you'd rather keep 6.

**The old dogfood recordings:** I don't think they're worth keeping.
- `run-E25HF5` is a one-off test run from 18 Oct, before the rebuild. It takes 127 MB, mostly saved desktop and review data.
- Its results and screenshots describe code that no longer exists.
- Its checkbox recordings were made while checkbox replay had a bug, which is now fixed.
- Nothing in the repo uses it except the handover note.

I'd delete the whole folder. It's under `.civic-canvas/`, so I'll only do it when you say yes.

**Remaining work:** three Codex workers have started, each in its own copy of the repo, with no commits or pushes from them:
1. [useEffect cleanup](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A9f43cd31-b115-413f-821e-100bc7675bb1%3Adelegate-task%3A833f054e-ec68-4af1-9fb5-fb00ce850095) cuts the 45 remaining calls down to the ones that really need it, and gives a reason for each that stays.
2. [Timers, sleep and wake, restart deadline](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A9f43cd31-b115-413f-821e-100bc7675bb1%3Adelegate-task%3A80427882-be6d-41f9-89ea-1a072aec1c48) does three things:
   - makes the host, desktop app and runs survive the machine sleeping;
   - tests the 60-second restart deadline;
   - removes the last 4 raw timers in server code.
3. [Shared sign-off package](t3-thread://v2/63e16fdf-a1e1-4363-8349-45c9a3b50bc1/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A9f43cd31-b115-413f-821e-100bc7675bb1%3Adelegate-task%3A75e326a4-b56e-49d8-a15e-a070bf0aa11d) copies Orca's `packages/signoff`, which now exists, into CIVIC and keeps CIVIC's machine-sharing wait. The package reads its settings from `main`, so the switch-over completes after it lands.

When they finish, I'll review their work, merge it as one batch, and run one sign-off.

**What happens to the rest of the list:**
- **The real-agent loop proof is next,** once a worker slot frees up. It means running a real agent through CIVIC's MCP server.
- **Orca-side wiring and the Orca and Laundry runs aren't mine:** I'm only allowed to read Orca, and the plan makes those checks yours to run.
- **The one-off viewport failure** gets covered when the workers run those checks again.
- **The ~3,300 lint findings:** I'd rather not mass-fix them. The lint baseline can only shrink, so the count can never grow back and they'll shrink as the code they sit in gets touched.

**Commit hooks:** they can be switched on now that the merge landed. That changes your checkout's git settings, so tell me if you want it.

import { Clock, Duration, Effect } from 'effect'

// Late ticks represent suspend or an unresponsive event loop, not proof of dead work.
export function awakeSleep(duration) {
  return Effect.gen(function* () {
    let remaining = Duration.toMillis(Duration.fromInputUnsafe(duration))
    let previous = yield* Clock.currentTimeMillis
    while (remaining > 0) {
      yield* Effect.sleep(Math.min(1000, remaining))
      const now = yield* Clock.currentTimeMillis
      const elapsed = now - previous
      if (elapsed >= 0 && elapsed <= 5000) remaining -= elapsed
      previous = now
    }
  })
}

export const awakeTimeout = (effect, duration, orElse = () => Effect.fail(Error('Operation timed out'))) =>
  Effect.raceFirst(effect, Effect.andThen(awakeSleep(duration), Effect.suspend(orElse)))

export const awakeClock = Clock.clockWith(clock => Effect.succeed(Object.assign(Object.create(clock), { sleep: duration =>
  Effect.provideService(awakeSleep(duration), Clock.Clock, clock) })))

- **The cause:** when the machine slept, every deadline in the host, desktop app and run supervision ran out the moment it woke. The host could shut down, sockets could close, and idle runs could be swept away.
- **The fix:**
  - Deadlines now count only time the machine is awake.
  - Liveness is still checked for real: a client that never answers a ping still times out.
  - Security deadlines like presence tickets still expire on schedule.
- **The 60-second restart deadline:** now tested. If a restart takes longer, waiting requests get a clear "try again" reply (a 503 with reload advice) instead of hanging.
- **Raw timers in server code:** down from 4 to 1. The last one is in the browser overlay, outside this worker's scope.
- **Checked:** 26 host and runtime checks, the managed-viewer checks on the first try, 21 desktop tests and 3 Electron checks all passed.
  - Sleep was simulated with clock jumps; nothing was tested through a real suspend and resume.
  - A long freeze also delays deadlines now, which I think is the right trade.

Still running: the shared sign-off package and the real-agent loop proof.

Both finished branches will likely conflict in the lint baseline file when merged. I'll resolve that when I build the batch, then run one sign-off on it.

import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { test } from 'node:test'
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { loadConfig } from '../tools/signoff/src/config.ts'
import { isSignoffProcess } from './signoff.ts'

test('matches actual sign-off script processes, not snippets or lookalikes', () => {
  for (const command of ['bash /repo/bin/signoff --no-post', '/bin/bash bin/signoff', 'node /repo/scripts/signoff.ts', '/opt/bin/node scripts/signoff.ts --fresh', 'bash "/repo with spaces/bin/signoff"']) assert.equal(isSignoffProcess(command), true, command)
  for (const command of ['bash -c "node /repo/scripts/signoff.ts"', 'node -e "bash /repo/bin/signoff"', 'rg bash /repo/bin/signoff', 'node /repo/scripts/signoff.ts.test', 'bash /repo/bin/signoff-other', 'bash /repo/notbin/signoff', 'civic-signoff-waiting']) assert.equal(isSignoffProcess(command), false, command)
})

test('the manifest keeps the existing checks and typed commit guard', () => {
  const config = loadConfig(readFileSync(new URL('../.signoff.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8'))
  assert.equal(config.typedCommits, true)
  assert.deepEqual(config.checks.map(check => [check.cwd, ...check.argv]), [
    ['packages', 'pnpm', 'install', '--frozen-lockfile'],
    ['packages', 'pnpm', 'run', 'check'],
    ['packages', 'pnpm', 'test'],
    ['packages', 'pnpm', '--filter', '@civic/graph', 'run', 'validate'],
    ...['demo/fluent-button', 'demo/card', 'demo/rebrand', 'projects/discovery-app'].map(dir => ['.', 'node', `${dir}/build.ts`, '--check']),
    ...['gate', 'release', 'browser'].map(name => ['.', 'node', 'scripts/signoff.ts', '--step', name]),
    ['.', 'node', 'packages/install.check.mjs'],
  ])
})

test('dry run explains optional steps and refuses posting', () => {
  const adapter = fileURLToPath(new URL('./signoff.ts', import.meta.url))
  const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [adapter, '--dry-run', '--browser'], { encoding: 'utf8' })
  assert.equal(result.status, 0, result.stderr)
  assert.match(result.stdout, /browser \(enabled\)/u)
  assert.match(result.stdout, /exit 1 is reported/u)
  assert.match(result.stdout, /with-temp-root\.mjs/u)
  const post = spawnSync(process.execPath, [adapter, '--dry-run', '--post'], { encoding: 'utf8' })
  assert.equal(post.status, 1)
  assert.match(post.stderr, /Posting requires/u)
})

content.text:
A real agent completed CIVIC's review loop end to end, on the third run. All four pieces of work are now merged into one batch, and its sign-off is running.

**Real-agent loop:** Codex, given only "use the CIVIC tools to find and complete the open work request", did the whole loop:
1. It listed the requests, read the one you'd left, claimed it, and changed the heading in a throwaway copy of the notebook example.
2. It reported the fix and did not commit.
3. CIVIC showed the fix waiting for you, and accepting it as the owner resolved it.

The earlier runs failed for reasons outside CIVIC:
- The worker's copy of the repo had no installed packages, so CIVIC's MCP server crashed on start.
- Codex's non-interactive mode refuses every MCP tool call unless that server is pre-approved. The test runner now pre-approves CIVIC's server for its own run only.

Two follow-ups for you:
- **Pre-approving CIVIC's tools for real Codex use:** CIVIC's Codex setup doesn't pre-approve its tools, so unattended Codex runs will hit the same refusal. Whether to change that is your call, because it means trusting every CIVIC tool without a prompt.
- **A small wording fix:** when the agent sent a stale version number, CIVIC refused correctly and the agent recovered. The error message points to the `civic show` command, though, when an agent would use the `get_request` tool. That's a one-line fix if you want it.

The runner is committed as an opt-in check: it runs only with `CIVIC_REAL_AGENT=codex`, because it spends model usage.

**Shared sign-off package:** I accepted the worker's result after three fixes:
- It had left a link to TypeScript using an absolute path into its own copy of the repo. I removed it so it wouldn't be committed.
- Orca's landing gate starts its sign-off in a form neither my old gate nor the new check recognised. That probably explains how the two sign-offs started together this morning. The check now recognises it, with a test.
- The new sign-off tests would never have run during a sign-off, because script tests were listed by name. They're now picked up by pattern: 19 tests.

**The batch:**
- **Contents:** the `useEffect` cleanup, the sleep-and-wake fix, the agent-loop runner and the shared sign-off package, merged into `candidate/batch8`.
- **The run:** it uses the new `bin/signoff`. Since `main` doesn't carry the new sign-off config yet, it runs the old steps behind the new quiet-machine wait and keep-awake.
- **If it passes:** I'll fast-forward the controller branch. Pushing to `main` waits for your go, as before.
- **After that lands:** the next sign-off will use the shared package automatically.

Leftovers I couldn't remove, because the safety hook blocks deleting folders and branches:
- **Temp folders:** the kept folders from the agent runs are in the system temp area, which macOS clears on its own.
- **Branch:** the `candidate/batch7` branch is still there.

content.text:
The batch passed sign-off and is on `civic/controller-2026-11-15`. Nothing new has gone to `main` or been pushed; your earlier go-ahead covered only the last merge.

**What landed** (in `4b45ae6c`, plus a handover update in `ee46550c`):
- **`useEffect` cleanup:** 45 → 41. Each remaining one syncs with something outside React.
- **Sleep and wake:** deadlines in the host, desktop app and run supervision now count only time the machine is awake. A restart that takes longer than 60 seconds now gets a clear "try again" reply. Server raw timers went from 4 to 1.
- **Real-agent loop:** the opt-in Codex run is committed, and it passed once.
- **Shared sign-off package:** copied from Orca and active. Its quiet-machine wait worked in this run: it held off until the machine was quiet, and the checks then took about 5 minutes.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **Merge into `main` and push again?** It would be a fast-forward of 6 new commits. Once it's on `main`, the next sign-off switches to the shared package automatically.
2. **Pre-approve CIVIC's tools for Codex?** Without it, unattended Codex runs will refuse to call CIVIC's tools.
3. **Delete the old dogfood run** (`.civic-canvas/dogfood/run-E25HF5`, 127 MB)? I recommended yes.
4. **Switch on the commit hooks?** That changes your checkout's git settings.

**Still open, not mine to do:**
- the Orca-side wiring;
- the Orca and Laundry trial runs, which the plan makes yours to run.

**Small, and I can do them if you want:**
- point the stale-version error at `get_request` instead of `civic show`;
- replace the last raw timer, in the browser overlay.

The remaining ~3,300 lint findings are left to shrink as their code gets touched.

The `candidate/batch7` and `candidate/batch8` branches are still there, because the safety hook won't let me delete branches. Both are fully merged, so you can delete them yourself or leave them.

content.content:
# CIVIC review from Orca

This is a proposal for the Orca controller. CIVIC makes no model calls, starts no
agents, and never calls Orca. Orca calls CIVIC through its MCP gateway.

Register `civic-mcp` over stdio in Orca's integration settings. Pass the selected
worktree explicitly as `cwd`. A work reference is `{ system, id, url? }`; CIVIC
treats those values as outside identifiers and knows nothing about Orca's types.

Offer **Review in CIVIC** on a work item. Call `open_review` with its worktree and
work reference, then show the returned link to the owner. CIVIC opens or attaches
the worktree's own preview. The owner comments there; each comment becomes a
request linked to that item. Subscribe to
`civic://requests?system=<encoded-system>&id=<encoded-id>` and read it after an
update notice. Route new requests through Orca's existing attention rules.
Keep the session ID and call `close_review` when that review ends; CIVIC must stop
only processes started by that session.

For a project Orca manages, offer **Make a work item** on unlinked CIVIC requests.
Read `get_request`, create the item in Orca, and call `link_request` with the
request's `id@version` and the new work reference. If the version is stale, read
the request again before retrying. Agents then use the existing claim, comment
and report-fix tools. Linking changes no review outcome.

Expose `changed_screens` and `coverage` through the gateway for the agent's current
worktree. Show screen, journey and backend coverage together, preserving missing
evidence and the reported limits. Subscribe to `civic://coverage/{project}` when
the owner keeps coverage open; unsubscribe when the view closes. Update notices
replace polling.

No coordinator action resolves a request, accepts a check, or writes an owner
annotation. The owner acts through CIVIC's review UI. Review sessions and links
carry context, never approval.

## Current implementation boundary

The MCP surface includes `changed_screens`, `open_review`, `close_review`,
`coverage`, work-reference links and request filtering. Request and coverage
resources support subscriptions; store file changes produce debounced update
notifications. Unsubscribe when the view closes; stdin end closes all watchers
and reviews owned by that coordinator connection.

Review sessions use `civic preview` and its process identities. A session that
attaches to an existing preview leaves that preview running when closed; another
session's ID cannot close it. The overlay reads the session's work reference on
the server and ignores a reference supplied by the page.

Tagged captures live in the repository's review store, under
`tagged-captures/<project-hash>/<scenario-hash>.json`. Each scenario replaces its
previous capture and records the preview inventory's source fingerprint. Screen
discovery uses only captures matching the current source and reports files with
no rendered tags. Opening a review collects missing captures with one browser
page, visiting scenarios sequentially. This establishes rendered synthetic
coverage, not real-device or deployment acceptance.

resources support subscriptions; store file changes produce debounced update
notifications. Unsubscribe when the view closes; stdin end closes all watchers
and reviews owned by that coordinator connection.

Review sessions use `civic preview` and its process identities. A session that
attaches to an existing preview leaves that preview running when closed; another
session's ID cannot close it. The overlay reads the session's work reference on
the server and ignores a reference supplied by the page.

Tagged captures live in the repository's review store, under
`tagged-captures/<project-hash>/<scenario-hash>.json`. Each scenario replaces its
previous capture and records the preview inventory's source fingerprint. Screen
discovery uses only captures matching the current source and reports files with
no rendered tags. Opening a review collects missing captures with one browser
page, visiting scenarios sequentially. This establishes rendered synthetic
coverage, not real-device or deployment acceptance.

content.content:
setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (code index, sessions, seed,
               docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO agent tokens. The
               brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. This is the first release in which
the watcher's --distill step and the session-end hook's distill actually run
(both were dead before), so setup is a real, recurring cost, bounded by five
gates: the fact phase ASKS before it spends (default no, and a run with no
terminal never spends unless --yes is passed), --backfill-budget sessions per
